Staying at this hotel was a life impacting experience, that I will never forget. Staying in a suite on the 61st floor, looking down at the pools at night, was a dream like experience. Housekeeping would come TWICE a day. Who does that? Top notch providers do that. Everything about my experience and my wife's experience at Fontainebleau was phenomenal. The Lapis Spa was incredible. My wife got the best massage she has ever experienced at Lapis Spa.  We took lots of photos and will cherish our four days at this hotel for years to come.

allReviews.title: It’s giving “The Price is Right”
allReviews.text: We usually always stay at Palazzo which we love, but we wanted to try the new spot in town. It was meh. It was a nice hotel, but for the price, there are better options. The  decor was boring and was giving  a mix between a mall and the set of The Price is Right. The pool area was probably their best asset. The eating choices were meh. We ate breakfast at Vida, which was pretty good. There wasn’t anywhere else exciting. They have a promenade with some fast food choices that were equally unexciting. The rooms were nice but not very spacious. We did have a nice view of the strip and the mountains through the floor to ceiling windows. The shower was small. Another drawback is our hallway smelled incredibly strong of weed our entire stay. Even though they have a strong no smoking policy.The absolute worst part of this hotel was the location. Not only is there little action on this part of the strip, but it’s across the street from the Golden Nugget which is very run down. You have to walk a nice long distance to get to anything else and the ambience in the area is depressing. Won’t be staying here again.

allReviews.title: Taste of Fountainblue Las Vegas only
allReviews.text: Recently tried 4 restaurants from the Taste of Fountainblue which started June 16- September something I think, similar to Canda's Summerlicious, i.e, set menu on a fixed price;1. La Fontaine-  $ 75.00 tip extra..we were 3 so tried all on the menu.deviled eggs, ok gourmand average; crude enjoyed by group; smoked salmon on brioche (bread not fresh-breaking apart) lemon hollandaise, very good; cheeseburger only touched the meat, fries were tasty but not hot; chocolate ParisBrest amazing as always, should be a bigger slice; soufflé pancake not as good as the last time...BTW all the meals came out so fast, we were wondering if they were already premade. Place was about 25 % occupied.2. Dons Prime - $ 125.- I think I did not pay for this; again with 3 of us we tried all on the menu;crab cake excellent as with the salads; filet mignon undercooked; halibut quite tasty; organic chicken not the greatest; brûlée was good.  Place about 30% occupied.3 Washing potato - $ 65. or $ 75. did not pay for this was disappointed with the amuse bouche of a pineapple bun ( all oriental bakeries have this); maybe soup or spring roll or something; nothing special about the dims trio; beef noodle , walnut shrimp and gailan please just get the walnut shrimp--BTW ver small portions....not worth to do this one.   50% occupied4 Komodo- ginger salad and salmon appetizer fresh and tasty,chilean sea bass was the best; not so much for the stir fry and mushroom noodles; with beans, rice and Brussel sprouts....everything was quite tasty but then minuscule in portions.   25% occupiedIt was a great idea and priced right for a 3 course meal, during this stay. Doing reservations on line was also not very good, since you do not get an answer right away. So we cancelled our online reservations and just walked in. Service at all were always great, filled water glasses and decent.It was a great attraction, so you have a fixed set price, and try the dishes. We are coming back agin in.August, to try the other restos.

allReviews.title: An Experience….
allReviews.text: My stay at Fontainebleau Las Vegas was absolutely amazing! From the fresh red roses in the lobby to the beautiful smells throughout the air Fontainbleau left no stone unturned… the room was huge, bed was comfy, the shower was fantastic. The staff were incredibly welcoming and went above and beyond to assist me with everything I needed. The food at Vida was delicious and sweet treats at Chez Bon Bon didn’t disappoint! I especially enjoyed the pools and wellness classes. If you’re looking for a luxurious experience look no further Fontainbleau Las Vegas is it! I highly recommend this hotel and will definitely be back!

allReviews.title: Family visit to Vegas.
allReviews.text: Wonderful, clean hotel with great dining and drinking options. Collin’s bar was amazing. Great atmosphere with the piano. Limited choice of machine gaming on the casino floor and pool a little crowded.

allReviews.title: Beautiful hotel, but lack basic standard needs
allReviews.text: no 24 hours pool, no sauna or steam unless you pay $180 to use the spa area,  staff is nice but is clueless anytime you ask them a question concerning the hotel, restaurants close way to early.  The hotel is very clean, they have a perfumish scent through the hotel(didn't like that at all, very nauseating)

allReviews.title: Poor quality and high price.
allReviews.text: To my disappointment, as I was checking to my room and it was not  clean. It had debris in the carpet and the night stand table with stains from the previous guests. The bathroom seem to have the same issues. After two calls to the hotel front desk they finally had it cleaned but not the night table, I had to clean it my self. The Dons restaurant service was good but not our steaks, again disappointment at their food. When we check out, I addressed the issue and what I received from the management they would look in to it. For a resort that supposedly is the high end it is not.

allReviews.title: The Fontainebleau Experience
allReviews.text: Fontainebleau gave me a 10/10 experience! Everything from the parking garage to the hotel lobby to the actual room was an A1 experience. I loved every moment I was on the property.  Luxury may be an understatement with what I experienced.

allReviews.title: Sister 21st Birthday 🎉
allReviews.text: 10 out of 10! Not only was this place stunning it offered luxury shopping along with great amenities all in one place! The decor was beautiful, both in the lobbies and bedroom. We had a great view which was towards the mountains so the sunrise and sunset was really nice. The pool was very very nice. This is a family friendly resort but trust me it wasn't bad.Even with the kiddos around it was still great vibes. I loved the bathroom the bathtub will have you falling asleep! Each room also came with a robe and complimentary slippers. Customer service was top tier as well! If you thinking about stor here do it! Promise you won't regret it

allReviews.title: mean service
allReviews.text: The casino managers are mean, they don't care about the customers. The machine are not functional. The hotel is under construction, made a lot noise.

allReviews.title: Love This Place
allReviews.text: There are very few hotels/resorts that I will stay at and not leave the property. This is one of them. Excellent overall experience with exceptional restaurants (Ito, Mother Wolf, Kyu, and Washing Potato) and a world class spa. .

allReviews.title: Overall a Great Resort with a Few Issues
allReviews.text: I’ve been to this resort twice and can truly say it’s my favorite on the Strip.The design is timeless and elegant….something you don’t find much in Vegas and with an equally nice crowd.The rooms were a highlight.  The resort is relatively new and everything feels fresh and clean.  The beds were sublimely comfortable.The location is a bit north of all of the action on the strip, which was a good thing.  There’s plenty of space to stretch out and breathe here.Probably the biggest negative was the lack of in -room coffee machines.  For the caliber of hotel, this was a big miss for the hotel and mission impossible to get a quick cup of coffee in the morning.  The resort should immediately add in room coffee machines as lines for the coffee shop were quite long.    Also, adding an on-site Starbucks/second coffeeshop  would be a no-brainer. The spa and gym are were also very good and another highlight.   Although the gym was well-equipped, it lacked a lot of basic machines (bicep curl) and closed everyday at 7PM…really unacceptable.  If the above issues are addressed, I would definitely stay here again.  Otherwise I might return to the Durango out in the suburbs.

allReviews.title: Nice views is a pretty place
allReviews.text: Is great pretty place they need to work in little thinks but over all good experience all the food places are great nice front desk and gym team

allReviews.title: Outstanding
allReviews.text: This is a lovely hotel on the north end of the Strip.   It is a 30 minute walk or short cab ride to Sphere. The property is very large, bright and airy.  Many of the rooms have excellent views, and they are spacious and modern.The fitness center is excellent, essentially a full gym, the pool area is lovely.  WiFi is fast.  There are many outstanding places to eat and a good food court as well.Finally, this is a price performer compared to other hotels of similar quality on the Strip.

allReviews.title: Major security problem mishandled
allReviews.text: I don't have often write reviews here, but I experienced an extreme security problem here that has left me shaken and incredulous. I was walking up to the guest elevators area, where there is a podium where security checks key cards for guests. A man walked up to me as I was approaching it, put his arm around me, and asked me to "have some fun." I said no and kept walking. He squeezed his arm around me tighter and said, "Come up to my room. I'll take you up." I pushed away and approached the security podium. He told security that I was his wife, was drunk, and he was taking me up to our room. I told security I didn't know him. Security then asked him if he was a guest. He said yes, showed his room key card, and gave them his room number. They then asked if I was a guest. I said yes, and showed my key card. They then asked for my room number, which I provided. They then asked me for picture ID.. They did not ask the man for his ID. I showed them my driver's license. They then said that I couldn't go up to my room. I was very confused, and security allowed him to keep squeezing his arm around me and trying to pull me up to his room. The restrooms were around a bend from this area, and I pulled away, telling security I'm going to the bathroom. I went to the women's restroom and called my work colleague, who was also in the casino. He came to meet me by the bathroom door and walked me back to security. When we got there, the creepy man was standing there waiting for me and saying I'm taking her to our room. My friend intervened and talked to security. Security allowed this man to get all the way to the elevator bank trying to get me to his room. At some point security decided to escore me up, and at that point the guy hopped in the elevators. Security escorted me to my room, where I bolted the door. Shortly therafter, there was banging on my door. I looked out the peep hole, and it was the guy. He would not have known my room number if security had not asked me for it in front of him. I called security and reported it. I then called another colleague who was also staying in our hotel. She stayed on the phone with me while he was banging on the door. As the knocking escalated, and no one showed up, she also called security from her room. Security gave her a hard time, saying that the call needed to come from the room that needed help. More time passed, and as I looked out the peep hole, the man had sat down outside my room. I called security again, and they said that they had sent someone up there to talk to him, but the guy said that he made an innocent mistake of knocking on the wrong room, so there wasn't a problem. Unfortunately the knocking continued and he was still out there. Much time passed with about 6-7 calls to security. Eventually security did come up, and while the security person was standing at my door, he received a message in his ear piece that the man was in the stairwell. They went to apprehend him. More time passed, and I couldn't get answers. Eventually security came back and said that they would move me to a different room. They said that they didn't apprehend him in the stairwell. Security told me to call the front desk to get the room assignment and then they would give me a security escort to a different part of the hotel. I then made many, many calls to the front desk. One person said, "What's wrong with the room" and another said I had to come to the desk to get the information (and I had to explain that security had told me to stay locked in my room. Eventually, and hours had passed by now, the front desk manager called to say that she was sending security up with a card key and new room to move me. Security then showed up and asked, "Where are we going?" He had no key card and didn't know where we were going. He called downstairs while we waited for a long time in the hallway to figure out what to do. Eventually I was moved to a different part of the hotel, many hours later. This should not be allowed to happen in a casino. When a woman says "I don't know this man," there is no world in which you question that. You do not ask a woman in front of a man who is squeezing his arm around you and pushing to provide her room number in front of him. And you don't take hours to solve a problem while a man creepily sits outside a woman's hotel room. It was a harrowing experience and no one seemed to care. The hotel is beautiful and we enjoyed some wonderful dinners here and afternoons by the pool, but no matter how nice a hotel may be, it's useless if not safe for women.

allReviews.title: Disappointed
allReviews.text: Careful if you book this hotel through American Express Platinum fine hotels and resorts, you might get there and they will wipe out your benefits. Platinum benefits do not book your airline at the same time you will lose your platinum benefits

allReviews.title: Fontainebleau 06/22-06/25
allReviews.text: Had a three night comp-stay (6/22/6-25) in a Gold room.  Observations follow:1.	Property remains beautiful.  Pretty much spotless!  Well done by all of the nameless (perhaps if you don’t notice) folks working tirelessly to keep things that way.2.	Table limits where $15 during the day, $25 evening for blackjack.  (Big change from $50 evening limits at the Wynn).  3-card poker opened at 9pm, at $15.  Sign of the times!3.	Multiple craps tables open all the time.4.	Resort and casino seemed busier than prior stays.5.	Miami Slice pizza good as always.  Capons Chicken, Won’t try again as chicken was only "meh" for me  .(only staff that asked me for rewards card to add points.  That staff member should be rewarded!).  Chez Bon Bon had usual quality offerings.  Smashed Almond Croissant was a genuine treat!  Tropical fruit cup also delicious!6.	Don’s Prime!  What can I say?  I have tried several LV steakhouses and this is my favorite!  The service is my stand-out…always attentive, professional, never intrusive…truly a cut above.  They offered a prix fixe (?) summer special, three courses for $105 (with a wine pairing for $65).  I chose the crab cake, with the most delicious sauce, the 9oz filet (side of creamed spinach – extra) and the best crème brule I have ever tasted!  The wine pairing included a delicious Heidsick Bubbles, A wonderful California cab and a lovely Sauternes.  Could not have been happier!  (and a good value compared to regular menu prices).  AND THE SERVICE!  I dare say you will not find a better team in Las Vegas!7.	Had very good fish tacos at the sports bar.8.	Let me say again that all of the staff had a smile, a greeting and were always working hard to make the guest experience top notch!  ( I state this as a long time Wynn/Encore guest, who appreciates great service.)9.	I mostly play slots and this casino has everything I look for!  Always some new games to try (and try I did!).  Also, good share of classic three reel/low volatility games).  As mentioned above, blackjack and craps were always open.  Three card poker, open at 9pm during the week.  Wonder 4 poker, weekends only.10.	I really like this property and hope more folks will give it a try!  It’s a real joy!Happy to answer questions!SteveO.

allReviews.title: Best hotel and resort on the strip by far.
allReviews.text: Everything about the Fontainebleau is top notch.  The rooms, restaurants, gaming and even the parking.  Great air conditioning in the rooms when compared to competitors.

allReviews.title: Anyone can do vegas, but the Fontainbleu is next level comfort.
allReviews.text: Fontainbleu is an exquisite exerience from the grand entrance to the impeccable rooms. Everything about the resort is next level from the cocktail program to the gaming. The pool(s) are beautiful and relaxing with cabana's and daybeds that we really enjoyed.

allReviews.title: Opulent accommodations and excellent staff
allReviews.text: I have only experienced this level of courtesy and professionalism from staff at one other place, and it was a Disney resort.  Everyone was incredibly polite and going above and beyond to make sure guests were having a good stay.  The accommodations were opulent (in my experience, anyway) and I had a terrific view.  The food was expensive (welcome to Vegas) but delicious.  I'd highly recommend this spot.

allReviews.title: Worth the money!
allReviews.text: It was a beautiful hotel!  Everything was clean and in order.  Beds were fluffy, not firm, which I liked!  Water pressure was spot on in the shower, but be careful, the water is hot if you don't test it before you enter.  I have some advice if you're on a budget, but still want this luxurious hotel:  If you're a coffee drinker, pack your own personal coffee pot and coffee pods.  I got mine from Walmart for only $16! Their rooms do not have them.  I also recommend getting snacks and water from the Walgreens across the street.  Unless you're rich, don't eat and drink from their mini bar!  There are ice and water machines on each floor, so you may want bring something to drink out of, like a thermos.  All in all, it was a wonderful stay!

allReviews.title: Best Hotel in Vegas
allReviews.text: This hotel is next level - Better rooms - Better service - Better food - Better ambiance- Just overall Better than anything else Vegas offers right now.

allReviews.title: Nice Room Hotel but need to improve in Casino Gaming
allReviews.text: The hotel facility was nice and the room was clean.  The only negative was there was no variety of Black Jack games.  The payout of blackjack is 6to5 instead of 3to2, no double decks games.The Ultimate Texas Holdem has the rules that the Dealer is getting the first card instead of the last one, which give the Player more concerns.

allReviews.title: Stay at the Fontainbleau
allReviews.text: The hotel was BEAUTIFUL and I loved their attention to detail (a fun game was finding the bowties in the decor. They're in everything!). The staff were friendly and helpful. I stayed in a "Royal Suite Strip Best View" room for 6 nights. The room was a nice size with 2 full bathrooms. The decor and furnishing in the room were beautiful as well. The view was GREAT! The bed and robes were extremely comfortable. All in all, I think it was worth it and enjoyed my stay BUT when I first got to the room, I noticed right away it hadn't been cleaned thoroughly. There were rice grains and paper from an open sugar packet around the kitchen sink, a piece of tissue in the fridge and melted water and a plastic bag in the ice bucket. This was surprising because I expect a freshly cleaned room from any establishment I choose to stay in, but even more so when I'm staying in a suite at a 5-star hotel.  I called the front desk, and they said they would have someone come up and "take care of it". I asked the agent to send them in a half an hour as I'd be gone, and they could have the rooms to themselves and was told my request was noted. Despite that, housekeeping showed up 5 minutes later, picked up the garbage, emptied the ice bucket, sprayed air freshener and left. After witnessing this, I took sometime later the next morning to more closely examine the room and further confirmed the room was not being cleaned properly. There was hair and debris in the corners of the room, the 'vanity packs' had been opened and left in the container and the AC vent was full of dust. I called the front desk again to explain the issues in full detail, hoping someone would understand my concerns and the principle behind it. I spoke with Renee, who expressed she understood my concerns, would send someone up to do a thorough cleaning and I could expect a call from the Manager of Housekeeping. She also stated that I had received $75 in resort credit towards food and beverages, for my inconvenience. Despite me requesting a specific time, I got a call from housekeeping 10 minutes later to say they were outside and had to request again they come back once I had left. I was still able to note the same exact debris in the same areas after the "thorough" cleaning, received no call from the manager and didn't notice any credits on my final bill. Only after this cleaning did I notice there were amenities (toothbrush, razor, mouthwash, etc.) provided that had not been during the "initial" cleaning. This was of no importance due to the fact that I didn't use any of the provided items but further proves the room was not being taken care of as it should have been. Room service was a bit slow (minimum hour wait, even just for wings) but it was the weekend, and the hotel was pretty busy.

allReviews.title: Great Start but needs to fix bathroom aerators.
allReviews.text: Had a weeklong stay in a Panorama Suite on this trip and had a weeklong stay in a Noble Suite on my trip in March of 2025.First thing to note is the arrival experience.  The valet can be extremely busy.  Drop off was smooth on both trips, but the traffic in front was a bit rough.  When you enter the resort, you are greeted by beautiful floral display.  To your right there is a VIP/Gold and above check in desk.  They are very militant about that desk.  On my first trip I had to go to the main check in and though the line was long the process was smooth and acceptable.  On my second trip I was up to Gold (Reward Status) and when I tried to use the VIP check in, I was told I wasn't allowed.  I had to login to my account on my phone to prove that I could use the VIP line which no one was in.  The standard check in was 30 plus people deep.  Even after I showed her, she was very snooty like I didn't belong.  The VIP check in was excellent (Aria Sky Suites level).  I had originally booked a Regal Suite and upgraded to the Panorama.  It was well worth it.The resort elevators are a short walk on tile from check in which is great.  Nothing worse than dragging your roller bag across carpet through a casino (Best reason to get a Wynn Tower Suite).  The Casino ceilings are super high, and it feels so open and comfortable compared to older resorts (Think Paris).  The elevators are quick and well thought out.Once to the room it was beautifully appointed and had amazing views.  Plenty of space to unpack and spread out.  The Panorama is an excellent choice for a couple that have different sleep schedules.  The living area is a good distance from the bedroom and very comfortable.  Room service coffee at the dining table or the living area is perfect.As a frequent traveler I can say my biggest beef with resorts often are the showers.  The water pressure in the shower is very impressive and makes the stay worth every penny. (If you have ever stayed at the Cosmopolitan, you know what I mean about the shower.  Hugh beautiful showers that have zero water pressure.)  My beef with the Fontainbleau is the bathroom sink aerator.  It puts the water out as a spray and it's a big miss.  Hard to rinse a toothbrush or razor.The Casino is great.  Plenty of table games.  I'm a craps player and they have both Craps and Crapless open most of the time.  They have a Bar that opens at 5:00 that has a Crapless table and quality drink service and is open every night ($25.00 Min).  Food options are plentiful and fantastic.  Spend the money and go to Don's Steakhouse.  Tavern Sports Bar has great food as well as the second floor food court (Possibly best burger in Vegas).The pool.  I did a Cabana on Friday and it was a great experience and the value was there.  Went down on Saturday to spend a couple of hours and there wasn't a single chair available on the entire pool deck.  Lots of empty chairs with Towels on them people were doing the old reserve for later move.  They need to get better about policing such activity (Wynn is the best at stopping this behavior).I would be remiss if I didn't say to stop by the No Where bar and get a drink from Reggie.  Best Espresso Martini I have ever had (and I've had way too many lol).

allReviews.title: Highly recommend.
allReviews.text: It was a great experience. The room was immaculate as was the service. It was a quick couple’s getaway weekend, so we mostly stayed in the hotel for our time. We ate at Mother Wolf and got drinks at Bleau Bar and I will be going back to both.

allReviews.title: Class & Comfort in the Fontainebleau
allReviews.text: Modern, classy establishment. Not cheap, but worth the splurge. Easy to navigate, unlike many of the strip hotels/casinos. It didn’t take half a day to reach self-parking! Well ventilated and little smoking on the casino floor. Courteous and friendly staff. Rooms were bright, spacious, and comfortable. Nice amenities in rooms: Clothes steamer, plush robes, slippers, toiletries, and chocolates! Bath tub was big enough to invite a couple of seals to do laps.

allReviews.title: Go to Fontainebleau! You will love it!
allReviews.text: If you are looking for a fabulous hotel with all the amenities you could want, you should absolutely check out Fontainebleau. It's beautiful, full of high-end shopping, restaurants, has a beautiful pool(s) and very comfortable, stylish rooms. I had a king room with strip view and it was only about $300/night (before taxes and fees) which was excellent! Room service food was fantastic (get the burger!) as was the food at our business conference. The casino isn't very big so if you are an avid gambler, this may not be your favorite spot, but if you enjoy playing the slots, there are plenty of those. When I come back to Vegas for pleasure in the future, I will probably stay here. I loved it!

allReviews.title: Splurge on yourself!
allReviews.text: The Fountaineblue in Las Vegas is an absolute splurge that everyone should experience at least once. The hotel, rooms and restaurants are on point. The Lapis Spa was an incredible experience from the Odessy massage to their saunas experiences and the salt room, exquisite.  Definitely worth every cent.

allReviews.title: Spend your summer at Fontainebleau...now!
allReviews.text: Amazing from start to finish. Checked in early, my room type wasn't available, but they found me something that was and waived early check in fee. Spent 3 days at the incredible pools - best in town with lots of seating and many shaded seats. Food was amazing at Washing Potato for dim sum and Papi steak was pricey but delicious. Got a $100 dining credit for stay. Amazing room rate deal as a member too. Amazing service at both. Slots and video poker were great fun and many bonuses a a couple good wins!

allReviews.title: The most elegant resort in Vegas!
allReviews.text: The most elegant and relaxing resort experience in Vegas! The only place we will stay from now on. Our suite was gorgeous and comfortable. Food was terrific, especially at Papi Steak. Casino was beautiful and welcoming. Pool was refreshing. We highly recommend visiting the brand new "Hall of Excellence" which showcases incredible memorabilia from the worlds of sports and entertainment. A must see!

allReviews.title: Nice place with great service! Pool costs are too high
allReviews.text: Fantastic hotel and casino with a fantastic pool. The only drawback is the very expensive drink menu at the pool. It out prices its competitors and that makes a difference for us that hang at the pool all day!

allReviews.title: Top-tier Vegas establishment
allReviews.text: Cleanest hotel, and casino in Vegas. I’ve been to Vegas about 25 times and this place is amazing. Tried about six different restaurants and shops and they were all excellent

allReviews.title: Absolutely the Best ‘Bet’ in Las Vegas!
allReviews.text: This is an updated review because I have since spent another couple days here, and I’m so further blown away that I just wanted to revise and add. My Las Vegas experience thus far consists of staying at the Mandalay Bay, The Four Seasons and the Cosmopolitan. This new Fontainebleu hotel, Las Vegas is in such a different league; there truly is no comparison.    I have been very fortunate in my lifetime to have stayed at some of the best hotels and resorts around the world, and this particular new Las Vegas hotel, when it comes to checking off all the boxes that could possibly be checked, takes the cake.   The location is fantastic, the aesthetics are unparalleled, all the food venues that we tried were absolutely spectacular. Every employee we encountered was phenomenal; and there are thousands of people that work here…    The room was beautiful, incredibly comfortable with a phenomenal mattress, excellent linens, excellent air-conditioning, fantastic shower water pressure, not to mention we were up on the 68th floor, so the view was extraordinary and it was as quiet as can be. I’ve been an Equinox all-access gym member for years, and the fully equipped health club here on the second floor is as nice (if not nicer) than any of the Equinox gyms around the country. Even the casino was fun, of which I usually do not spend any time in. And they have an enormous, clean and safe, easy-to-navigate through self-parking facility attached to the hotel which is just fantastic for those of us who sometimes prefer not to be fussed over at check-in or check out.  This hotel helped me fall in love with Las Vegas this trip, and we are happy that we are moving back to the West Coast so we’ll be able to come here with frequency for a quick getaways.  I truly cannot recommend this hotel enough, not to mention that it can be even less costly than some of the other, above mentioned Las Vegas hotels that I’ve stayed at previously.  Special mention to Delfa at Front-Desk/Check-in, she is exceptional, a true gem; the hotel is lucky to have her.  Also special mentioned to Ashley in The Tavern.    Thank you Team Fontainebleau, we look forward to returning soon!

allReviews.title: One-Star Review: Disappointing Customer Service at Fontainebleau Las Vegas
allReviews.text: As a local military member, I frequent resorts up and down the Strip, and I've consistently experienced outstanding service everywhere—except at the Fontainebleau. While it's a beautiful resort, the customer service, particularly concerning military members and locals, is severely lacking.Every other hotel on the Strip acknowledges and appreciates military service by placing us on a higher tier, a privilege we never take for granted. The Fontainebleau, however, uses the same tired excuse that they don't offer such a program yet, despite having been open for a considerable amount of time. They also fall short by not offering tier matching, a common practice among other casinos.My family and I may not be high rollers, but we regularly enjoy dining, shows, and concerts at Strip resorts. Given the well-publicized issues Fontainebleau has had with customer loyalty, you'd think they'd make more of an effort to improve their standing with locals. Instead, it feels like they're just digging a deeper hole.With so many other excellent options available on the Strip that genuinely value their guests, especially the local military community, I'll unfortunately be passing on the Fontainebleau this year.

allReviews.title: Not a 5 star resort or experience.  Too much cost cutting to try and stay afloat but that has ruined things.
allReviews.text: Not a 5 star resort or experience.  Too much cost cutting to try and stay afloat but that has ruined things.

allReviews.title: Top notch resort
allReviews.text: We had a great time here. If you are looking to be with a mature crowd away from the chaos of the strip this is the place to go! The food was excellent and the amenities were on point. Room was spacious with excellent views. Conveniently located with easy cheap taxi rides to wherever you need to go.

allReviews.title: Move over, Cosmopolitan
allReviews.text: This might be my new favorite hotel in Vegas. You feel like you're in the lap of luxury as soon as you walk in.The common areas are beautiful and the casino is great. I was pleasantly surprised that some of the slots and table games had low minimums. Of course, if you want high limits, there's plenty of those.The pools were nice. They're family friendly, but not to the point that I felt annoyed. There's a 21+ pool too, but it was dead most of the time. That's fine though, as I was mainly there for the hot tub. I didn't get a chance to go to Liv, but it sounded like a vibe. Maybe next time.

allReviews.title: Best hotel in Vegas!
allReviews.text: This casino and hotel are as nice as any of the luxury hotels on the strip, and a much better value. Rooms are large and new and the staff is too notch.

allReviews.title: Best spot on the strip!
allReviews.text: I know it's a little ways down the strip, but I have stayed at Fontainbleu 3 times now, and each visit was exceptional. The staff is friendly and helpful, the rooms are clean and beautiful, and the restaurants (especially Mother Wolf and Miami Slice) are some of the best in Vegas.

allReviews.title: FB wknd get away
allReviews.text: Hotel was everything we expected it to be. It is at the end of the strip but has so many amenities you don’t need to leave the resort at all. We had the strip view from our room, can even see the Dome and room was slightly larger than other king rooms. Restaurants (Papi Steak, Mother Wolf, and Vida) plus in room dining were also all great! 21+ pools could use livelier music choices but all in all, great stay!

allReviews.title: The best hotel in Vegas
allReviews.text: The Fontainebleaus Hotel is by far the most beautiful hotel in Vegas. We would book it again and again. The rooms, the staff, the pool area, the casino, the gym it's just all right. Thanks for this fantastic stay!

allReviews.title: Really fantastic hotel.
allReviews.text: Very nice hotel. Great ambiance. Excellent service   Great food and amenitiesBest gymExpensive with some nickel and dime charges that are unnecessary at this price point ($10 to deliver wine glasses to the room)

allReviews.title: Luxe Aesthetic, Clean Vibe, and a Bit Out of the Way
allReviews.text: Fountainbleau is a good option if you're looking to get away from the chaos of the central Vegas Strip. It's a large, modern resort located at the far end of the Strip, kind of off on its own. It has just about everything you'd expect—plenty of restaurants, bars, a casino, spa, shops, a big pool complex, and LIV (note: both the club and pool have entrance fees).Once you're there, it really doesn't make a lot of sense to head back down to the busy parts of Vegas. It’s more of a self-contained experience—convenient in some ways, isolating in others.Pros:- The room was spacious, stylish, and clean. Easily one of the nicer rooms I’ve stayed in for the price.- The whole place is bright, smoke-free, and doesn’t have that heavy, stale-air feel most Vegas hotels have.- Pool area is impressive, and there's an adults-only pool that’s actually peaceful (rare for Vegas).- If you book through Amex Fine Hotels & Resorts, you get a few solid perks like breakfast and early check-in/late checkout.Cons:- It’s far from most of the action. You’re looking at a longer Uber ride to Strip spots like Bellagio, Caesars, etc.- Restaurants were pricey—not just “Vegas pricey,” but noticeably higher than similar places on the Strip. Papi Steak in particular felt like style over substance.Avoid:We were invited to make a reservation at the Poodle Room, which is a “hidden” lounge they pitch as exclusive with the best view of the Strip and Sphere. Honestly, it was nice but totally dead. Drinks were overpriced, and the vibe just wasn’t there. Wouldn’t recommend unless you're just curious.

allReviews.title: A Luxury Respite on the South Strip
allReviews.text: First class venue removed from the crowded North end of the Strip. If you looking for upscale elegance and quiet this is great venue — except when LIV Beach is happening on Saturday afternoon.

allReviews.title: Best Experience
allReviews.text: Besst Resortg every - amazingt and A+ from check in to check out to Rewards Program - it was excellent all through - I would not hesitate to receommend this resort to all - try it and u will fall in love ! Rooms are modern and classy with all amenities thorougly thought thru

allReviews.title: Not worth the price, better options south
allReviews.text: Rooms are pretty nice. Tough location to walk other places. You’re stuck w captive restaurants which are fine but not great. Great gym. Service overall below what you’d expect at other similar venues. For example we had no hot water one morning after waiting 5 minutes. Called and they said the hotel was full. Wait longer. Ok, fine, but that doesn’t happen at Holiday Inn when I’m paying $800 less per night. Overall it’s fine but I wouldn’t go back. Better places if you’re happy spending $1000 a night.

allReviews.title: Very impressive
allReviews.text: The best stay we have had in Vegas to date. Everyone is extremely helpful and friendly and the rooms are very clean. The beds were so comfortable it made me want one for our home:) Next time I’d like to try more of the restaurants but we did dine in The Tavern food was very good. Definitely looking forward to our next visit

allReviews.title: Overall Would Stay Again - but definitely areas for improvement
allReviews.text: As a Front Office Manager with several years in the hospitality industry, I always appreciate experiencing other hotels and wanted to share my feedback on my recent stay at the Fontainebleau Las Vegas. I was in Vegas celebrating my 28th birthday and attended two shows at LIV and LIV Beach which were conveniently located at this property which is why we chose to stay at the Fontainebleau. Positives:The property itself is stunning—modern, luxurious, and beautifully designed. We had a great view of the pool despite being only on the 8th floor, and the key-access requirement for guest elevators was a fantastic touch for security. Pool access was easy, and the beverage service was on point. The Promenade food hall had a solid variety of options and was convenient for quick, quality bites. I also want to give a big shout-out to housekeeping—our room was serviced exceptionally well on the day we requested it.Areas for Improvement:Unfortunately, several aspects of the in-room experience fell short. The drapes didn’t fully close, the rainfall shower head wasn’t functioning, one of the lamps didn’t work, and the beverage cooler barely chilled the drinks we purchased. I brought this up at check-out, and while I understand issues can arise, a simple apology or acknowledgment from the front desk staff would’ve made a difference—especially since these should have been caught during room inspections.Additionally, the service from most staff members (excluding the valet team, who were great) lacked warmth and engagement. Eye contact and a friendly tone go a long way, but we experienced minimal guest interaction. Even at check in, and there not being a line, our check in contained minimal conversation which is a great way to connect with the guest and start their trip on the right foot. We also had checked our luggage and went to get it before heading upstairs and said we could bring it ourselves so the gentleman got our cert and began unloading all our items, keep in mind we had 5 bags and a box for the two of us and when asked if we could use the cart we got a fairly rude response of “no, that’s why I asked if you wanted to bring your stuff or if you wanted us to bring it up.” I understand not wanting guests taking the carts because they may never make it back for other guests, but it would have been appreciated had that been made clear when we requested our bags to begin with. We could not have brought all the items by ourself so we had to go up to the room then call the bell desk to have our items brought up and when I gave the representative our ticket number and room number he called us a different guests name… this caused immediate concern as to if we would be getting our bags. Ultimately, we did about 30 minutes later, the agent called me back and said “hello, just wanted to let you know we switched the names on your room so you are all set now”, shouldn’t that have been immediately done when we were checked into the room and given keys? Another instance was a call to request bandaids resulted in a short, dismissive response and a 25-minute wait.Overall, Fontainebleau has the potential to offer an exceptional guest experience, but a stronger focus on room maintenance and genuine service culture would elevate it significantly. The property is stunning and we did overall love the stay, but the interactions we had with the staff both at the beginning of our stay and towards the end, did sour it a little bit. But, that being said, it is a newer property and still figuring it out. Our experience would not deter us from staying again.

allReviews.title: "Overpriced, Unsanitary, and Fraudulent Charges — Avoid at All Costs
allReviews.text: 🔥 **Fontainebleau Las Vegas Review**⭐ **1 Star****"Overpriced, Unsanitary, and Fraudulent Charges — Avoid at All Costs"**My recent stay at **Fontainebleau Las Vegas** was one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had — and I travel often. I booked two rooms (one prepaid, one financed through Expedia) expecting luxury and received nothing but **stress, filth, and unauthorized charges**.Upon arrival, I was told to pay an **additional $850 per room as a “deposit,”** even though one room was paid in full and the other was secured through Expedia. When we entered the rooms, we were horrified:* Hair shavings in the sink* Dirty rugs* Hair on the bathroom floor* A **used tissue** left in the nightstandWe checked out in **less than 24 hours**, and I was assured by the front desk that I’d only be charged the resort fee and taxes — totaling $62.50 per room. **Minutes later**, I discovered **$604 per room had been charged to my card** without explanation.I immediately returned to the front desk and was told the charges were a mistake and that the refund would be processed. **No refund has ever arrived.**I reported this to **Expedia**, who then blamed the hotel — while the hotel blamed Expedia. Neither took accountability, and both have caused me emotional and financial frustration.Fontainebleau may look flashy from the outside, but behind the scenes, it’s mismanaged and dishonest.**Unclean rooms. Dishonest billing. Rude management. No integrity.**Avoid this hotel — there’s nothing luxurious about being scammed.

allReviews.title: I’ll never stay anywhere else in Vegas!
allReviews.text: By far the best LV hotel I’ve ever experienced. The vibe is light and bright. Everything is CLEAN. The rooms are amazing (get the Strip view) and the shower was to die for. We loved getting a private cabana at the Oasis pool - VIP check-in, outstanding service/food and welcome shade. The entire place is amazing. Don’t miss their French patisserie for an early morning coffee and croissant.

allReviews.title: Great stay
allReviews.text: The hotel is beautiful with a mountain of fresh roses in the lobby that get changed often (we're told).  High end shops and restaurants are all over. The rooms are big and clean. The AC is a bit loud but not enough to prevent me from sleeping. We were on the 28th floor so we had a great view. Speaking of views, the Sphere can be seen when standing outside. Fontainebleau is located a few miles away from the common/popular hotels on the strip. We Uber most of the time but it is a walkable distance.  Aside from how expensive the restaurants are, the area where our room was located had a peculiar/unpleasant smell that never went away. I should've asked for a different room but instead I dealt with it because I didn't smell it inside the room.

allReviews.title: A must stay in Vegas
allReviews.text: If you are looking for a new, clean, and exciting hotel in Vegas, this is where you want to stay. The restaurants options are endless and the hotel staff are so friendly. We only had to leave our hotel for a few business meetings.

allReviews.title: Conference at Fontainebleau
allReviews.text: Fantastic property, both the rooms and conference area. The shops and eatery's were top notch. Little loud but overall great experience.

allReviews.title: Best spot on the strip!
allReviews.text: Our experience was the best we have ever had on the strip. We found our new home! From the dealers to the restaurants, not a better place to spend a weekend with friends!

allReviews.title: Excellent hotel great tourism, highlighting its concept and luxury in each of its facilities. Don't stop visiting
allReviews.text: Excellent hotel great tourism, highlighting its concept and luxury in each of its facilities. Don't stop visiting

allReviews.title: Luxurious destination resort!
allReviews.text: Exceptional experience!  Fontainebleau is a destination resort, with luxurious rooms, restaurants, and pools.  The Nowhere Lounge features top jazz musicians nightly.  All of the staff ate well dressed and professional with a smile.  Cheers!

allReviews.title: Love the Miami Fontainebleau, but the Fontainebleau Las Vegas Needs Major Help!
allReviews.text: I expected the hotel to have a 5 star experience like the Miami hotel, but this one was soulless and without question the most painful luxury hotel bed I've ever experienced.  I'm in Vegas a ton, and it would take a major change to go back to the Fontainebleau.  I've never had a luxury hotel where I leave with neck and shoulder pain due to a bad mattress and specifically awful pillows.  This hotel has an amazing shell and bones, but it feels soulless and needs an internal refresh.

allReviews.title: Fountainbleu June 2025
allReviews.text: Rooms are amazing-fresh and new. Super clean. Modern and up to date. Great views of the sphere and the city in general. Checking in was very easy. Jeremy at the check in desk was awesome. The casino floor is super clean and well lit. Restrooms on the casino floor were clean. The Tavern restaurant/sportsbook has amazing food. Definitely recommend the Prime Rib French Dip sandwich. It was the best French dip I think I have ever had. The auju was perfect. The meat was so tender and finely sliced. Definitely two thumbs up. Parking garage is super easy to get in and out of. There are several other casinos within walking distance. We loved this place!

allReviews.title: A Beautiful Hotel in a Less Desirable Area
allReviews.text: This hotel is luxurious and the rooms meet the standard.  Positive points are that parking is free for guests.  (I read it somewhere on the website, but it wasn't that obvious.)  The location is irs main negative.  That area of the stripstill has elements  of seediness.

allReviews.title: Great Experience
allReviews.text: Beautiful hotel.  Fantastic service.  Food was impeccable.  Would highly recommend for a person looking for luxury without the nonsense further down the strip.  Very classy experience without the high price of the Wynn.  The pool was a great mix of families and singles.

allReviews.title: The best hotel in Las Vegas, Fontainebleau
allReviews.text: Great in...- Service- Room - Overall decoration- AtmosphereMy first time in Vegas and this is the first impression I've got from this city, Fontainebleau Las Vegas! Thank to my team who decided choosing this hotel for 9 nights. Moreover, the bar, casino and food court were so great!

allReviews.title: Not all new is good
allReviews.text: A hotel that is still really green in service and attitude. Has a lot to work on before competing with the other hotels on the Strip. Beds were super uncomfortable, service was terrible, zero politeness.They don't try to make an effort on guests experience.

allReviews.title: Hotel/Casino in Las Vegas, NV
allReviews.text: Overall a pretty, clean and spacious casino!  Didn’t stay here but came to check out their casino and grab lunch Sunday.  La Fontaine is a good place to eat at!  Casino wise, lots of slot machines and tables to play—wasn’t crowded at all (daytime).  One thing that needs improvement is cocktail service—we played at the slot machines for a while and no cocktail waitress came by for drinks—all the other casinos we’d been to all weekend had plenty of servers come by.Location wise, this is a bit far from the main area strip and is a bit more secluded so it’s not as lively/energetic area.  They offer valet which was $40.  Lobby had beautiful pink red roses as decor, so pretty!

allReviews.title: Fantastic hotel experience!
allReviews.text: Fantastic place! Highly recommended. Beautiful, clean, quiet, excellent customer service, fantastic food and different options. It is far enough from the main, loud, super busy, and sometimes dirty strip, but also close enough to go anywhere. Swimming pools are also great!

allReviews.title: Elegance and class is what this hotel is .
allReviews.text: Elegant and classy, from the pool to the service everything was fabulous. the restaurants are phenomenal. It’s at the end of the strip which is great because it’s not crazy busy with people coming to look at it. We absolutely loved it. We will be back

allReviews.title: Best resort in Vegas.
allReviews.text: Excellent stay overall. I will be back.They bend over backwards to make sure you are completely satisfied. Rooms are a pleasure to stay in,everything is provided. The views were awesome from my room on the 50th floor.I will highly recommend this resort.

allReviews.title: Best hotel in Vegas
allReviews.text: Best hotel in Vegas , clean, beautiful, modern, great restaurants, nice common areas . I would definitely recommend this hotel to friends and I would definitely come back for my next visit. The rooms are spacious and very comfortable. The best hotel.

allReviews.title: 2 star service, 5 star price
allReviews.text: We got a great deal on our room; if I had paid list price on my room I would NOT be writing a three star review - it would be much less. Our room was supposed to be ready at 3 and it wasn't ready until nearly 5pm. The check-in desk was kind but when we asked what the issue was they couldn't give us an answer and offered nothing for the inconvenience besides keys to the pool (which we would have had regardless). We travel fairly extensively and I honestly can't think of a time that our room wasn't ready on time and certainly not 2 hours late. The hotel is beautiful and clean, staff is very kind, but I think they're understaffed and the air in our room wasn't working well. We ate at Vida for breakfast and sat at the bar, I had to ask the bartender multiple times for refills of water; my cup was sitting right where he was working - it was a little annoying to have to draw it to his attention. But again, I think he was just overwhelmed/overworked. The staff was doing a terrible job checking keycards to get into the pool and to get up to the rooms. We went to the pool and ordered tequila, soda water, lime with extra limes and got lime juice with tequila in it (one lime). Our waitress was wonderful and did make it right though :). I would have been WILDLY upset if I had paid the normal going rate for the type of service we experienced.

allReviews.title: Much like Cosmopolitan
allReviews.text: As a VIP customer, I found that the treatment at Fountainbleau was not as accommodating as other hotels like Bellagio/MGM or Wynn. The room was adequate at best and the bath products were used and had not been changed from the previous guest. The hotel is much like the Cosmopolitan in that it is for a young crowd not a gambling crowd.

allReviews.title: Had a great time
allReviews.text: Very comfortable rooms and happy with the way everything went service was very nice too the pizza and tacos are amazing too id definitely go again if I’d stay anywhere in Las Vegas it would be here and the pool too it’s very nice and big service there was great too

allReviews.title: Fresh and fun
allReviews.text: Gorgeous hotel with fresh, modern amenities,  beautiful layout, and decor. A breath of fresh air on the strip. I stayed for a short weekend trip and enjoyed the spa which offered a serene, relaxing and luxe experience. I will absolutely be back and highly recommend staying here!

allReviews.title: We love the Fontainebleau !!
allReviews.text: Really fabulous  hotel.  Much less smoky smelling than other Vegas hotels. They work hard to keep that smell out of the hotel and we love that.  Fabulous employees.  Everyone is thankful and appreciative that you are there and they let you know. Very clean hotel.  PLEASE keep it this way !!  We stay in lots of hotels ... usually under the Marriott umbrella.  The Fontainebleau has the best hotel beds and pillows we have ever had the pleasure of sleeping in.  I want to buy the mattress for our home.  We are Tempurpedic people but we actually love the mattress, pillows and the linens at this hotel.  We usually eat at Vida for brunch daily and the service and food there are good.  Ask for Aya !! She is a true gem.  We had dinner at Mother Wolf and it was good.  The cocktail we had was very nice.  The pasta is homemade but they were so busy our food came out lukewarm.  That was odd.  We live in Austin and have a lot of Italian restaurants that are better.  My husband says the hotel gym is very good especially for a hotel.  His only issue is he wishes it was open later -- it closes too early.  He likes to be able to work out at his convenience and that might be early or later.  This is an overall wonderful place to stay in Las Vegas.  It is at the end of the strip but we actually love that too.  Feels safer.  We will be back !!

allReviews.title: Best hotel room I’ve stayed in
allReviews.text: The rooms are a 10 out of 10. It’s just a beautiful room that was comfy linens are comfy. Everything about the room was a 10 out of 10. Everything was high tech, which was really cool. Bathtub was huge, check-in service was great. The bar, waitresses and pool bar waitresses not so friendly but maybe if you’re a man they will be. other than that it was a really beautiful hotel

allReviews.title: Nice, but needs several fixes
allReviews.text: Stayed here twice, I have some Pros and Cons:PROS:Location-some say its too far away from the main strip area; for me I lOVE this, away from the massive crowds around the Bellagio area. Woke up early Sunday morning, walked over to circus circus, got my Starbucks, and kept walking to Resorts World (very close and my favorite hotel in Las Vegas) and kept walking. Cheap mini-mart convenience store right across, and only a few miles from DTLV. And 1/2 mile walk to Bagelmania; what more can you ask for?Pool- Besides the terrible pool food (and ridiculously overpriced) its one of the best pools in LV hands down. Spacious, many areas and decent music. Free ice water dispensers everywhere too. You'll need it or be ready to cough up $40-50 for drinks.Gaming- I feel like I'm gambling in an airport or airplane hangar, but the game varieties have improved. They have only 1 single double deck table, but a couple tables with popular freebet 21 (called something else here I forgot) but easy to spot. $25 minimums were available throughout the day, and even $15 in mornings.Food- besides again, the awful pool food, Komodo and Chez Bon Bon are terrific (fancy Asian and 24hr pastries/snacks/drinks/gelato). Many other nice restaurants and a very nice food court with ample seating and a view of the casino floor.Free parking for all guests...this should be standard but most charge.CONS: Room bedsheets had stains, inexcusable. The mattress is easily the worst thing I've every slept in 50 years of my life, like a sinking marshmallow. However, rest of room clean and quiet.Pool food- As stated twice, worse quality than a gas station. Had the worst fries and chicken tenders in my life, couldnt eat after a few bites they were reheated garbage, disgusting and very overpriced. So, fix the beds, clean the sheets, serve non nuked food at the pool, and offer more double deck 21 and freebet tables. Also waaaay too many slots need more classic video poker machines with better payouts. Lots of open wasted empty space. Size is just waaay too big, and finally got the hang of the North/South parking garages...dizzying.

allReviews.title: Would Recommend
allReviews.text: Beautiful hotel/casino with excellent service, very friendly and helpful staff.  The Casino restaurants and bars are all unique and excellent, the hotel room was very modern and comfortable.  I was really impressed with the Casino staff at the hotel and restaurants, they were all really friendly and helpful.

allReviews.title: Fontainebleau is where it's at!
allReviews.text: An absolutely incredible experience from beginning to end! Friendliest and most attentive staff anywhere on the strip! Beautiful rooms with comfortable beds and great water pressure in the shower. Highly recommend a massage and spa day. Mother Wolf is a standout in a huge lineup of great food.

allReviews.title: Great experience.
allReviews.text: Amazing place. A must in Vegas.Spacious, new, spotless, great people.Some of the words that we could use to describe our stay at Fontainbleau.The pools had had plenty of people but you still don’t feel overcrowded.Would go back again and agian.

allReviews.title: Fontainbleau Resort Las Vegas Shines Like a Diamond
allReviews.text: Excellent hotel. End of the strip. A somewhat hidden gem. It is actually a HUGE hotel and so glamorous and classy. Wonderful restaurants, shopping, pool, conference facilities, and rooms. I loved the room I had on a high floor. The view of the desert and mountains in the distance was magnificent. The staff at the hotel were all very customer-service oriented and professional. Great hotel, the Las Vegas twin of the Fontainbleau Miami Beach. Both are great properties and I recommend both. The Las Vegas property is actually newer, even nicer, and has a massive casino and so many cool bars, eateries, stores onsite. I could see people checking in for a weekend and not having to even leave the property!

allReviews.title: Worst. Stay.
allReviews.text: This is the worst stay ever. First, when I checked in, she had the wrong checkout date, which sent me into a panic attack, but when I checked the next morning, it was what I initially thought it was, not what she had told me. She must’ve been new. First two days I had my light on privacy and the housekeeping still came in and moved my pajamas to the dirty table. My curling iron was wrapped up. You’re not supposed to wrap curling irons up like that. I called them after the first day and told them I did not want them in there and they still came in the second day. I don’t know if there’s a miscommunication or what. Plus the privacy sign is very stupid and it looks like it’s a reflection of the exit sign right across from it so you really can’t tell Unless you put your hand over it that it’s on privacy. Like stop being fancy and just get a door sign that hangs over the door handle like normal. I also don’t like the bottles that the shampoo conditioner and body wash come in. It’s really hard to get the liquid out of those. I was also missing $40 worth of Starbucks gift cards when the housekeepers came in. I thought not to report because whatever it’s only $40. Now I’m thinking maybe I should’ve .  I called to let them know again. I do not want people in my room.Third day I couldn’t get in my room so then I went downstairs to reactivate my key. They reactivated it. Came upstairs. It did not work. Had housekeeping call Security. Security came his fab did not work either. They called engineering for the first time. Engineering came and to open the door fixed it or so we thought, the keys worked. I grabbed my stuff for work inside the room and left in a hurry to get to work.   I was late because all of the work computers were in the room and I couldn’t get in my room. After work come back to the room the key is still not working. They call engineering AGAIN.  Engineer comes up, supposedly fixes it, I have to leave to drop stuff for work off at a storage unit and drop my friend off at the airport. I get back. I talked to the front desk, she comes upstairs with me to make sure it works, it does NOT.  Again.  I have to go back downstairs and they obviously have to give me a new room because the door is broken. Shouldn’t maintenance check those doors and when the battery goes to 40% replace the battery for the door key? I have never had this issue in any hotel .  I get the new keys to the new room, but I Still have to wait on engineering to get in the room to get my stuff to then go to the new room. This was the THIRD time Waiting on engineering to get in my room.All they offered was to take off the resort fees. Shouldn’t I get a comped stay out of this in all the hassle I had to go through?  I tried but the lady Manager downstairs on June 4 was very snotty and catty and didn’t really give a crap.  I could tell when she was reacting to the hotel staff when the hotel staff was explaining what was happening with me in my room. I saw her roll her eyes. But then when I’m standing in front of her, she did not do that. Still is very upsetting.  Also, I have stayed here before in February and it was not this complicated though. I did have an issue also in February when they didn’t even know where to send me to pick up or drop off my Hertz Rent-A-Car. I feel like that is something the front desk should know.  They had no clue where I should park it to return it.Overall, a terrible experience. This is coming from someone who stays in hotel rooms all the time. I usually stay at Marriott and Hilton’s in Hyatt because of my status. But even when I did not have status, I’ve never had this many issues. I also do a lot on social media and cannot wait to make a TikTok/Reel about this.Apparently, the owner of this hotel is losing money and doesn’t care because he’s so rich. That is the rumor. It trickles down from the top!I check out tomorrow. We shall see how that goes.

allReviews.title: Luxurious and Relaxing Experience
allReviews.text: This resort is the epitome of luxury and comfort. The rooms are spacious, clean, and have incredible features even for the standard King Bleu rooms! The casino downstairs is lively enough to have a good time while maintaining an elegant feature. The restaurants are exquisite and you cannot skip Mother Wolf. The various wellness services offered are top knotch including IGK hair salon, IV drip (perfect to cure a hangover), and a beautiful looking spa. You won't ever regret staying here

allReviews.title: Wonderful resort casino
allReviews.text: Overall fantastic casino resort with a true resort feel. Enjoyed dining at Mother Wolf, The Tavern, and Washing Potato. Collins has fantastic artisan cocktails with friendly and fun bartenders. Also caught live music at No Where Bar with a band doing covers and standards.The fitness center is clean with many equipment choices. Pool is beautiful and kept at a great temperature.

allReviews.title: Best Hotel and Casino on the strip
allReviews.text: The best and newest hotel on the strip. It's light and bright, not dingy and dark.  Being from Florida I feel the Miami Beach influence.  The staff is 5 star from the moment you walk in the door. Even the standard room is bigger than most hotels upgrades.  The clientele is high end and classy sophisticated.   We are locals and go there often for dinner and events. Every restaurant there is excellent as well.   Best omkase on the strip in my opinion.  Views from the top floor as you enjoy the sushi

allReviews.title: Great Casino
allReviews.text: Fountainblau is an amazing Casino, beautiful spacious and everyone courteous and efficient. we enjoyed our stay immensely. The casino floor is very nice La Fountain restaurant is exceptional. The room was amazing great view. The check in very easy.

allReviews.title: Class act!
allReviews.text: Best Casino in Vegas from an experience and stay standpoint! Amenities are top notch, great restaurants and pool vibes. Lapis SPA is truly the best spa experience I have ever had. Rooms were really high class with great products in the bathroom.

allReviews.title: New Hotel, Friendly Staff, Excellent food and a fun Casino
allReviews.text: The bed was so comfy and the room amenities were outstanding.  Large soaking tub, robe etc.  I am use to staying at the Cosmo which is loud and Aria and the beds here were tops.  Place is beautiful We had the Beef Chow Fun at the Washing Potato I would Highly recommend.

allReviews.title: Never leave the property!
allReviews.text: This resort was everything one could ask for! The staff wanted to please at every turn. The rooms and facilities were beautiful and well maintained. The pools were numerous with chair-side food and drink service as well as bars nearby,  the workout facilities were very nice and well equipped. The restaurants food, service and variety were spectacular! I never left the property!

allReviews.title: Amazing stay in Vegas at the best hotel
allReviews.text: We love to stay at the Miami resort so we wanted to stay at the new Las Vegas hotel and it did not disappoint.  Just walk through other resorts in Vegas and you will appreciate Fountaineu Blue that much more.  Great atmosphere, great rooms and restaurants.

allReviews.title: 1st experience and stay at Fontainebleau
allReviews.text: I just checked out this morning (Monday 6-2,) after enjoying a long weekend visiting with family that live  in Henderson.  I have stayed at  several hotels on the strip and decided to stay here for the first time, and, the Fontainebleau is hands down now my favorite! I checked in on Friday 5-30 and a huge shoutout to Front Desk Agent, Delfa.  She was very friendly, professional , and answered many questions I had regarding the property.  I was upgraded to a suite on the 24th floor with an awesome view.  The room was spectacular.  Thank you Delfa for that great customer service!I will definitely be staying at the Fontainebleau on my next visit to Vegas!  What an amazing experience and a few of the other hotels on the strip need to step it up because the Fontainebleau has now set that bar pretty high.  Thanks again and I’m looking forward to my next stay.

allReviews.title: A beautiful resort with many options
allReviews.text: Beautiful resort, great room view of the city and sphere. Gorgeous room. Bed and pillows so comfortable! If I didn’t want to check out Vegas I’d stay in the bed all day! (Besides popping down to the pool!) Gaming available of course but we are not gamblers-but looked like others were having fun. Many different types of restaurants available. A decent variety of types and prices. Valets helpful with taxis, concierge helpful with suggestions when asked.

allReviews.title: Amazing hotel!
allReviews.text: Wow - this is my new favorite hotel in Las Vegas!  The property is stunning - just gorgeous!  We enjoyed Bar Collins, Bleau Bar and No Where and most of all Don's Steakhouse!  Do not skip on a cabana at the pool.  We were so well cared for by Ray, Deshawn and Chris.  Seriously - we had a day of heavenly relaxation.  The rooms are spacious and so beautiful!  Bathroom and amenities are top notch.  Can not wait to return!

allReviews.title: BEST place to stay in Vegas!
allReviews.text: We have traveled to Vegas MANY times and stayed at several different places, so we decided to give the Fontainebleau a try and we were SO HAPPY we did!! We arrived about 2 hours before their posted check in time and we had not requested an early check in, but that was no problem! We also requested a different room type and again, NO PROBLEM! We stayed in room 6261 and it was perfect! We had a GREAT view of The Sphere - which was so fun to sit in bed and watch it! The bed was comfortable and the room was spacious. I was so thankful for the refrigerated drawer so we never opened the mini bar. TIP: Walk across the street to the store by Circus Circus and get some drinks to fill your fridge and save some serious money! The bathroom was beautiful and the water pressure was seriously the BEST I have ever experienced at a hotel! We enjoyed meals at Capons (the burger was big enough to split between two of us and we shared the yummmmy truffle fries!). We ate the hot honey pepperoni pizza at Miami Slice (pricey - but hey, it's Vegas!), and guac and chips and an amazing chorizo & egg burrito that they serve all day at Roadside Taco. The pools were great and if you want a quieter scene, take an immediate left (after you grab some towels) and go to the adults only pool. You can't take any coolers or other drinks in the pool area (Even if other guests claim you can, they check bags at the door) but no one looks in bottles if you bring a drink inside of a closed bottle. There are water stations around - so it's nice to bring your own bottle to refill with water. It was a really great weekend at a beautiful hotel. Take a chance on the Fontainebleu! You won't regret it!

allReviews.title: Another stellar visit
allReviews.text: Another outstanding trip to the Fontainbleau. Have had the pleasure four times and was able to return over Memorial Day weekend with my teenage daughter. I was worried about the party scene, especially at the pool, but was pleasantly surprised how family friendly it was. Everything was great from check in to check out. We had a beautiful room on the 53rd floor with a downtown facing view. We celebrated her birthday with a dinner in Dons Prime which was also wonderful. As always the gambling was fine. Still hate that the blackjack tables pay 6:5, but was pleased to see affordable minimums even on the weekend. My only complaint was how slow the elevators were. I don’t think it could be helped because the place seemed very busy, but it took 10-15 minutes to get an elevator we could fit in while waiting on our floor. Already booked to return in August and can’t wait to return.

allReviews.title: Fun pool day!
allReviews.text: The pools at the Fontainebleau are fantastic -- we had a day pass to the resort and took advantage of a 100-degree day in Las Vegas. It's very laid-back vibe during the week but excellent service (check in with Javier, the bartender, and his crew).

allReviews.title: amazing view
allReviews.text: The hotel looks very impeccable, but in my room for the price I found some dusty and dirty objects like the tub ñ, I found some hairs, there was a toothpick forgotten on the floor, for the price you pay if I find it expensive, I got a room with an amazing view, I don't think it has a bad location, but if I would go back to that hotel, as far as the bed is very clean

allReviews.title: Don’s Steakhouse
allReviews.text: My family and I went to dinner at Don’s steakhouse and it was absolutely phenomenal! The weight staff didn’t miss a single beat. The entire dinner was a celebration of a special family event and they pulled out all the snoops. It was the most memorable experience than I’ve ever spent at any restaurant anywhere you are definitely coming back.

allReviews.title: Fantastic but expensive
allReviews.text: The Fontainebleau Las Vegas is an upscale, pleasant, friendly, and gorgeous new hotel.Staff was very friendly, pleasant, and professional throughout - from check-in, to room service, to restaurants, to poolside, to housekeeping, to checkout. A+ for staff and service.The room was very clean, a nice size, with attractive decor and useful furniture pieces. The bed was super comfortable and the shower was awesome! Great water pressure and heat. In fact, enjoying the water pressure of the shower was one of the small pleasures of the stay. A+ for the room.Main casino floor is gorgeous, with excellent ventilation. I hardly ever smelled any smoke though people were clearly smoking. They don’t have a poker room (which I would’ve liked), but seem to have everything else. Casino floor felt fun but also spacious and non-crowded. Rideshare areas are convenient and well-marked. A for the casino.Pool was also awesome, with a neat layout, and multiple pools. They even had a fun little movie night on Sunday where they played Top Gun on a screen. A for the pool. Got a couple strawberry daiquiris and they were really good, albeit expensive ($24 for one 12oz). And I think the cheapest beer was like $9?Which brings me to the only real drawback about Fontainebleau -  ALL food and drinks are expensive. They have a food court, but it’s upscale and pricey too. Want a quick couple slices of pizza and a bottled water? That’ll be $34. Chicken sandwich, fries, and a coke? $46. And I’m just talking about the food court. The little grab and go coffee shop was also the same. Ate a single meal in the sportsbook and got room service one night - both those meals were $70-some dollars. The food tastes good, but make your peace ahead of time with the fact that it’s all very expensive. So B for food options.I could afford it and was OK with it. And I know it’s Las Vegas, but it was honestly still kinda exhausting after 2.5 days to have no escape from the high food prices. So for this reason, for me, the value proposition overall wasn’t quite there to give them a full five stars. But if they’d mixed in a few low-cost options, I would have easily given them five stars. If anyone from the hotel is reads this, if you would consider adding just a few  lower-cost options (maybe 1 restaurant, one coffee shop, and one low-cost alcoholic drink at the pool), that’d go a long way towards making the stay more comfortable. I’d still eat in one of the more expensive restaurants, but giving us the ability to mix it up would be greatly appreciated.That said, overall I had a great stay and really enjoyed the Fontainebleau. I’d consider staying here again. And btw FLV, Resorts World, and Encore/Wynn, there seems to now be a critical mass of good stays, eats, and shopping in this northern end of the strip - another plus. It’s also walking distance to The Peppermill.So if you want an upsacle, gorgeous, friendly and fun experience, Fontainebleau Las Vegas is a great option!

allReviews.title: Roland & Debbie 33rd wedding anniversary at Fontainebleau
allReviews.text: 1st time stay at Fontainebleau.  Yes, we will visit this resort again! Outstanding Pool Deck. Gaming area was clean. Plenty of professional and friendly staff throughout the resort.  Parking was easy.  Access to our room was easy.  Plenty of dinning options throughout the resort.  Room was clean with a great view of both the mountains and the Las Vegas Strip.

allReviews.title: Great option with modern amenities
allReviews.text: Was at the property for a corporate event. Everything was managed well except that my room was not ready when I arrived around 3:30 PM. They took my mobile number and texted when it was ready which took couple of hours. The room that was eventually allocated was on the 70th with great views. Their housekeeping team does a great job, food at the event and the one meal we had at one of the restaurants were all nice. The staff was well trained and were polite & helpful.

allReviews.title: Amazing!
allReviews.text: Highest quality resort in Vegas.  Will not stay anywhere else!  Room was outstanding.  Best showers ever!  Resort not crowded.  Super luxurious and not expensive for what you get.   Komodo restaurant is an awesome experience!  We stayed at another resort for part of our visit to Vegas and are so disappointed that we didn’t stay at Fountain Blue the entire time.

allReviews.title: Best hotel in Vegas.
allReviews.text: This place is amazing. Clean, organized and the staff so accommodating. The lobby is beautiful. Checking was a breeze. The staff was so caring and amazing. The room was spacious and clean. The bathroom was huge. I will certainly come back.Bye Bye Resort World

allReviews.title: Cheap Service !!
allReviews.text: Worst experience. We booked 3 month in advance we asked for a higher floor since we have an infant. They gave us the lowest floor. So it was noisy all night and smell vigarettes, we talked to a manager she did not care. We had to leave and go to the wynn where we usually go. Wynn made our stay better and even upgraded us to a suite when they heard our experience about fontainebleau. You can build luxury but it s not easy to provide a luxurious service!! Staff needs hospitality management classes

allReviews.title: Such a shame !
allReviews.text: It’s such a shame about this hotel. The hotel itself is beautiful and the casino is nice. The Housekeeping is a disgrace, stay a second time here and encountered the same issues, unclean room and very poor housekeeping, on this occasion they could not move us due to the hotel being full. The room had long black hairs all over the bathroom, mouldy taco of some sort in the chilling drawer, which housing keeping came to remove and did not bother cleaning the sauce from the chill drawer. No cotton wool in the vanity pot and toiletries were very limited. This hotel is supposed to be 5 star and clearly isn’t in terms of cleanliness, get this sorted Fontainebleau!!

allReviews.title: Wonderful
allReviews.text: The Fontainebleau is really a gorgeous and immaculate resort-casino. The staff was incredible from the minute I pulled up to the valet,  till the end of my stay.  Everyone was so helpful and inviting. It's hard to explain but the energy that the Fotainebleau radiated was wonderful. The food was excellent and I highly recommend the Hangover Hamburger at the Tavern in the Sports Book.. I highly suggest bringing your workout clothes and taking advantage of their excellent fitness center. Afterward, be sure to relax beside one of their many crystal-clear pools.My stay was well worth every minute spent there, and I honestly didn't want to leave.

allReviews.title: Fontainebleau 4 U!-YES!
allReviews.text: The FontaineBleau-from the moment you exit your vehicle.   To the moment you walk into your style of room.   You will find Elegance.  This New Hotel is special.   They did not skimp on service for their Guest.   A MUST Stay.   Oh!  And remember to visit Chez Bon-for breakfast, and adore their BowTie Croissant.

allReviews.title: Great Hotel, worth every penny
allReviews.text: The feeling I got when entering my room is priceless! Just gorgeous, innovative and comfortable. The hotel is pricey, but it is worth every penny. The hotel is new and exudes elegance which creates such a great experiences.My favorite restaurant is la fontaine, exquisite, fresh and delicious.

allReviews.title: Hooked!
