It’s such a shame we couldn’t spend more time at the resort.  We will be checking out early.  We look to forward to returning if and when the ‘fragrance’ is no longer used.

allReviews.title: Honest impartial review from an experienced traveller
allReviews.text: The good:The hotel itself is immaculate. The staff professional and attentive. The food is good. Cocktails are on point.The bad:Possibly it’s due to the time we were there, SEMA week, however: restaurants are all always busy and a wait. Bars even worse. Get fed up and ate elsewhere several times.The ridiculous:The Lapis spa, incredible property, treatments were superb. HOWEVER, and again, perhaps it was due to the week we were there and the clientele present, but the coed area was filled with loud, obnoxious clients. Remarkable a facility like this wouldn’t enforce a quiet policy.

allReviews.title: Terrible customer service
allReviews.text: We heard good things and decided to try this new Vegas property. The room is fine, but on the small side. The restaurant options are good. But they are clearly still trying to figure out their customer service. We went to check out the pool and learned that’s it’s closed for construction. Any credible hotel will let you know about construction when you book your reservation. We called guest services about this and spoke with two supervisors. Both had quite an attitude and said it’s not their policy to let customers know about pool closures. I asked about crediting us back the resort fee given that the main pool area is closed and they refused. Oh well. There are so many nice properties in Vegas with good customer service. No reason to settle for one that doesn’t understand what good customer service is.

allReviews.title: Amazing casino
allReviews.text: Beautiful experience, very clean and staff was great. Definitely the best casino in the strip. Room was spacious and their food court areas was great, great delicious choices to choose from. Would definitely recommend and choose this casino for my future visits.

allReviews.title: Nice room, not so great service
allReviews.text: I had high expectations because the hotel is so new and the overall Fontainbleau brand, however a lot of annoying lapses in service happened during our stay, listed below. I did really enjoy the restaurants on site, especially Washing Potato and Mother Wolf. And the room itself was really nice with a great view (from the 69th floor). Small but annoying experiences: - Housekeeping did not come even after we pressed the service button. We had to call to request they come. When they did come, they did not remove our in-room dining items. They also did not tell in-room dining to come clear it. So we came back to the plates still there and had to call again to have them removed.- Internet did not work after the first day of our stay. Impossible to connect both phones and laptops. - When we checked in, we were given late check out because of our Amex Platinum booking. I told the staff member we were going to check out at 4pm and she noted it. However, on the day of check out, our room keys stopped working in the afternoon. We were locked out. I asked a woman from housekeeping for help but she refused to help me. It was only after I basically begged her to call her manager that she helped. She refused to let me use the phone in a room that was unoccupied. She also couldn't give me the phone number of the front desk. It was only when her manager arrived that we were let into our room. - Maintenance and painting of the hallway started on our floor. We weren't given any notice of this. It was noisy, smelly, and blocked the hallway. - The main pool deck was closed. We weren't given any notice of this prior to our arrival. Ridiculously, we were still charged the resort fee. - Unacceptable that there isn't coffee in the room. - The small bottles of shampoo and body wash in the shower was very difficult to use. The bottles are too hard to squeeze so it's very difficult to dispense liquid. Not practical and very wasteful to have single-use plastic like that in every room.- A lot of shops are closed or boarded up and not yet open. It feels very empty walking around the first couple levels of the hotel. - Check out took too long. The combined check in and check out lines meant we had to wait with newly arriving guests. The line was 4 rows deep. The staff member who checked us out made errors on our final bill that I had to spot and correct. This also took a long time. - We were not told how to exit the car park after check out. We were stuck at the gate and had to wait for a staff member to arrive to tap their card to let us out. This surely can't be the most effective way of guests leaving the car park after they've checked out. While none of these are really that terrible on their own, the fact that they all happened to us on a short, 2 night stay isn't really acceptable.

allReviews.title: A five star resort
allReviews.text: A conference at the Fontainebleau brought my husband and I in October 2024. We were super impressed with the hotel. Every single staff member was friendly and so helpful. Honestly, the staff was probably the best I’ve ever encountered at a resort. It’s a beautiful resort and smells AMAZING!  Our room was quite large for a standard king and the bathroom was very nicely appointed. The bed was extremely comfortable too. We spent 6 nights here and explored many of the restaurants and we were not disappointed with any of them. We liked that there were so many dining options on site.  Some might not like the distance from the main part of the Strip, but we didn’t mind that. We liked the quiet. We enjoyed that the casino was not filled with smoke, like so many others. We will definitely stay here again!

allReviews.title: Great hotel, BUT.............some disappointment!!!
allReviews.text: I actually would have given our stay a FIVE, except a couple problems.  After staying there 6 days, five nights, spending several $1000s, Sunday our flight departed Vegas at 4:30, I called guest services and requested a late check out until 3:00 instead of noon.  They charged me $125, said we could not stay until 3:00 unless we paid $125 (did I mention we had spent $1000s over the week?).   I told her that was not fair, she said she couldnt do anything.....very unusual lack of service for any Vegas hotel.Secondly, we were in a Noble Suite, GREAT VEIW, but the furniture is small and uncomfortable....couch is like of love seat, cant relax and chill to watch the sunset.  Lastly, none of the fine dining is open late.  WE MAY OR MAY NOT TRY IT AGAIN.

allReviews.title: New but very raw
allReviews.text: Terrible place service is very bad, awfully crowded, disgusting service and awfully expensive not delicious restaurants. Especially surprised breakfast, was a tight line, $150 bill for two and not delicious. In the tea room casino cheap chips on the tables . In general, there was a feeling that the hotel was opened not ready for further work with guests , of the pluses probably only good rooms , large enough and beautiful , but it is not a hotel 5 stars ...

allReviews.title: Best hotel vibes on the strip
allReviews.text: Best hotel in Vegas, great food and service.  Mother Wolfe was amazing.  Hotel staff and service is second to none.  The spa is amazing and made us feel so good.  The beds are comfortable and pillows are amazing.   We will be back as often as they will have us.

allReviews.title: Wonderful stay!
allReviews.text: Gorgeous room and so many wonderful little details that added up to a wonderful stay! We have stayed at some very fine hotels, and I would definitely rank this one up in the top three hotel stays!  Check in was a breeze, loved the casino and the bars are top notch!

allReviews.title: Best Resort on the Strip.
allReviews.text: The most beautiful resort on the strip period. Pair that with the best set of restaurants, great gaming, beautiful rooms, and an incredible spa, what more could you ask for.  So many hidden gems, I find new things every time I come. Can't wait for my next trip.

allReviews.title: Best hotel on the Strip!
allReviews.text: Fantastic hotel! By far the best hotel I've stayed at in Las Vegas. Hotel was spotless, room was fantastic, staff was extremely nice and helpful. Worth every penny and I can't wait to go back and attend another concert in the incredible concert hall.

allReviews.title: Bonkers amazing!!
allReviews.text: I stayed 1 night and had an amazing time.  I went to the Oct 30th Tears for Fears show.  The bed was delicious and the pillows so soft. The promenade is a spectacle  all on it's own with the art and flowers. The staff were so attentive and kind.  I'd do it all over again but stay a couple nights next time.  I just loved it!!

allReviews.title: The newest kid on the block, is the best in vegas in the last 20 years!!
allReviews.text: It is the best Casino Resort on the strip and the best I have been to in years!! The facility is beautiful, big and awesome.  The service top to bottom was 5 star, the rooms were very big, well appointed, will the finest linens and towels.. The casino was expansive with games and ranges for everyone.  The slots were the newest and the best. The food offerings was outstanding

allReviews.title: Amazing
allReviews.text: Everything was amazing the staff the hotel was really nice and clean. Smelled amazing, I did not have one complaint. The room was very spacious and everything was upgraded of course. I loved the real roses they were everywhere. Room service was good also.

allReviews.title: Awesome and Clean
allReviews.text: Very clean, new and great fun.Was there for Tears for Fears concert in the theatre. While far more upmarket than most Vegas properties it also has maybe older client set. Also a little more on expensive side but ok as not as crowded. Service was ups ale. Ate at Mother Wolf really good.Probably has best hotel gym I have ever been in.Tavern/sports book was good and unlike some properties on the strip they do not hit you up for a beverage minimum if there for NFL on Sundays

allReviews.title: Beautiful hotel, well-thought-out room lighting
allReviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, very stylish without being gaudy. Prompt and friendly car valet service, they even charged my car (after signing a consent form). My favorite part was the in-room lighting controls. Very high-end glass control panels, and great features like room scenes, bedside controls, a nightlight in the bathroom and a dimmer on the vanity mirror. The shower is huge! I wish it had a shower wand - that is my only (Very minor) wish. I stayed in a Gold room.

allReviews.title: Fountainebleau Vegas Shining Diamond Experience
allReviews.text: This is a must visit first class resort style hotel, check in, pool area, rooms and room service dining was above and beyond for the nightly price in comparison to other hotels on the strip. Advice for those that have sensitive skin to request a humidifier and wear single layer nurturing lotion, it will help with the Vegas dry air and AC in the various venues. You won’t want to leave this facility once you spend an evening there, every room have floor to ceiling windows capturing the strip and sky of either early morning sunrise or evening bliss of sunset.

allReviews.title: Friends weekend at the Foutainbleau Las Vegas
allReviews.text: Beautiful hotel, excellent accomodations, great restaurants, best work out facility, with free pilates classes and tons of equipment, rooms were attractive, clean and very comfortable. Service was terrific! The pools and outdoor seating areas were very attactive and there was ample seating and lounges. Overall a great place to stay!

allReviews.title: Fontainebleau experience - Las Vegas
allReviews.text: Very welcoming. Spacious room, great view. Fantastic gym facilities.Plenty of dining options available - promenade food hall was good for relatively quick bite; sushi etc in Komodo was delightful; good breakfast portions in Chez Bon Bon.

allReviews.title: Huge Disappointment-Luxury just not for you.
allReviews.text: Disclaimer, this was my first visit to Las Vegas.  The list price for a basic room at this hotel during my visit was north of $800.  So I had high expectations for comfort and luxury.  What I experienced was something very different.FIRST IMPRESSIONS We entered the built from the far side, and were greeted by security staff who very politely directed us to the lobby.  It took a while to traverse the shopping and casinos to reach the lobby. The building is grand and beautiful. The floral arrangements and artwork are beyond belief.  The lines for checking in were long, and moved quickly.  The desk clerk was efficient and waived an early check in fee, but also would have allowed us to store our luggage at the bell desk.  Everything, was great.   Or so I thought.  When I looked around the lobby, I noticed there wasn’t a single place to sit, no benches, no chairs, no couches.  There was a hard plastic ledge alongside one of the planters between the lobby and the elevators.  But where could an elder or a weary traveler rest?  In front of a casino machine.  It struck me—the lack of seating was intentional and despite the fact that millions of dollars were spent on the lobby—-nothing was spent on the comfort of guests.  I asked the concierge if I could get a razor as I left mine at home.  THE ROOMThere was no offer of a bottle of water, piece of fruit—nothing.  The elevators are quick and frequent.  The room key worked.  The room was as promised—-two queen beds., a dresser with medium sized capacity. There was no fridge, microwave, coffeemaker, balcony or desk.   Clearly not appointed with the comfort of the guests in mind.  There were very expensive amenities for purchase —and for which I was charged despite never having used.  The room appeared fairly clean, however when I went to put my clothes away I found the floor of the closet to be unvacuumed and quite dirty.  The  same when I looked around the edges of the roomThe bathroom was spacious  with tub shower stall, two taps (one big sink basin).  And a toilet in a separate enclosure.  The toilet needed to be flushed three times to fully flush down No. 2.  Water pressure was adequate, it often took a long time to get hot water.  The towels were of moderate quality.  The toiletries were similar.  Oddly the shampoo, body wash and conditioner were in small bottles (not the typical pumps found in  modern hotels seeking to minimize environmental impact. The bottles were so rigid and the product so thick thst it was almost impossible to dispense.  Like trying to get ketchup out of a glass bottle.    Clearly not well thought out and not in the interest of the comfort of the guest.OTHERThere really want much else except the pool which was off opened only from 9am-6pm.  There is what I can describe as an unusual level of scrutiny of the guests bags-/just to insure no outside food or beverages were brought in.  Security actually build some guests the could not bring coffee purchased on the second floor into the pool. There were no staff assisting guest in finding or setting up a chair.  It was a free for all of getting through security and running to a vacant spot.  Reminded me of a concert—not a luxury hotel.  Lastly the most disturbing part of the visit was the experience I had with the residents of another room.  Late one evening I heard a screaming child in the hall and came out to see if everything was okay..  the mom “apologized” as they were just playing.  I suggested they play in their room or in the downstairs areas it was disturbing, Hours later I hear a child screaming again, put on a robe and went into the hall, a father was throwing his child in the air.  I said that it was late, I was trying to sleep and it was very kid and disturbing.  Several doors opened, and others added their voice saying the same thing. The dad, and an uncle told me to mind my f-ing business and approached me threateningly.  I returned to my room called security but never heard what happened.  Didn’t feel safe or comfortable.  No follow up from Management.—so disappointing.

allReviews.title: Welcoming elegance.
allReviews.text: I am a local but I’ve been staying away from the strip because of parking fees. I just discovered that Fontainebleau has four hours of free parking.  We went Thursday and were back today. The hotel ambience is elegant and tastefully done. They have restaurants open for lunch  that has sophisticated service and upscale dining  atmosphere. And the car exhibition are piece of art. I think I found a place where I could hang out whenever I need a place to go.  One more thing- they are arguably the best hotel food court in Vegas. - teaaroundtheworld

allReviews.title: An ok stay but won't be in a hurry to return.
allReviews.text: A difficult review for me as I want to be fair:  obviously a very new hotel and the room was v comfortable however there were a few niggles:  the elevators are a LONG waĺk from reception which I found weird, the car valet pick up was at a different to valet drop off, and again a long walk away, the food prices were on the high side and finally, having paid for a strip facing high floor room, I was a little dissapointed because despite being on the 62nd floor, my strip view was largely blocked by the Encore Hotel.  I had no sight of any hotel on the east side of the strip and only down as far as Ceasars on the west side, although I did have a good view of the Sphere.  All in all, nothing not to like, but equally I wouldn't be in a hurry to return.

allReviews.title: A Resort not to miss
allReviews.text: The most amazing experience with customer service. Everyone was eager to help. The room was sparkling clean. Great choice for restaurants which were reasonably priced. The complimentary fitness classes were flawless. Unfortunately the spa services were very very expensive. The location is in a good area for walking and felt safe with all the security. The size of the room was enormous and the soaking tub was just what I needed

allReviews.title: Looking for luxury? ... then Fontainebleau should be your choice
allReviews.text: Staying in Suite 65-21 was nothing short of incredible! The view alone is breathtaking, offering an unobstructed panorama that truly makes you feel on top of the world. The suite is outfitted with high-end amenities that elevate the entire experience—every detail has been carefully considered. The bed was superbly comfortable, and I have to say, the pillows were the fluffiest and softest I’ve ever slept on, making each night a restful retreat. Being a newer hotel, everything is immaculate and luxurious, which only enhances the sense of a premium stay. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a perfect blend of comfort and elegance!

allReviews.title: The most beautiful new hotel in Las Vegas
allReviews.text: The Fontainebleau, which opened this year in Las Vegas, was a lovely surprise. We were in LV on business and took an afternoon to explore the hotel. As a designer, I was deeply impressed by the thoughtfulness of the design which permeated the whole property, including lobbies, retail areas, restaurants, and bars. It's big, and tall and impressive, but also calm and sophisticated. Definitely worth checking out!

allReviews.title: Sticker Shock
allReviews.text: Beautiful hotel, good food, comfortable beds and spacious rooms, but all highly overpriced. Pool was closed. limited table games with very high limits. Guests charged for valet parking, although when I called the hotel before coming they told me parking was free, but they didn't clarify that was only self parking.Service was great everywhere.

allReviews.title: Mother Daughter Trip
allReviews.text: Great hotel to bond with your adult child. The beds were firm and soft. The robes were a nice amenity. The building and people were very attentive. The food at Mother Wolf and Don's Prime was cooked to order and melted in our mouths. I did miss an in-room coffee machine :)

allReviews.title: Great Stay at the Fontainebleau!
allReviews.text: The hotel is gorgeous. The spaces are expansive and dramatic. I had a standard king room and it was much larger than the average room. The toiletries smelled amazing smelled amazing. Everything in the hotel was very clean and of course new. The  pool area was very pretty as well. I went to the pool in the mornings as it started to get crowded by Eleven o'clock or so and hard to find a place to sit. All of the food that I had was good as well as the service. The staff I interacted with were very nice and helpful. I would definitely recommend staying at the Fontainebleau.

allReviews.title: Beware of Theft in your room!
allReviews.text: Warning, I had $1,500 stolen from my room. The hotel security team didn’t care to do any sort of investigation whatsoever. They wouldn’t tell me on the phone if my room was accessed by hotel staff and told me to file a police report so they can then subpoena for the records. Filed the police report and haven’t heard back. STAY AWAY. I don’t think they hired the most competent of staff. Will never stay there again. I’d say the only positives was the sushi bar upstairs in the food court, high quality and not offensively expensive.

allReviews.title: Be careful
allReviews.text: Customer service should’ve been a lot better. Make sure that you check your receipt upon checking out because I was triple charged and room service is very expensive so I would just be very very careful. Make sure you stay on housekeeping to make sure your room get cleaned

allReviews.title: Great hotel!
allReviews.text: This property is beautiful, comfortable and clean. One of the best hotels I've ever stayed at. Casino is great, restaurants were awesome and the location is perfect especially if you came for the football game. I will definitely be staying again .

allReviews.title: Don't Arrive Hungry If Checking In Late
allReviews.text: Checked in after midnight after long flight from Florida was starved but there was no open restaurant besides Chez Bon Bon which has very little offerings besides were out of 75% of the items on the "menu." I've never stayed in a major casino that didn't have a full sit down 24 hr restaurant availableAlso no convenience type store on premises, Walgreens was a 4 block walk in not a great neighborhood.Besides that hotel was beautiful and stay was wonderful.

allReviews.title: The Best
allReviews.text: Just outstanding!!!The resort experience is the best on the strip, having stayed in just about every resort along Las Vegas Bl. The casino floor was clean and smoke free making it feel healthy. The resort atmosphere make you feel secure. Will definitely be on top of my goto resort on the strip. My host Jen was professional and very helpful.

allReviews.title: Get Here Before Everyone Else Does
allReviews.text: This hotel is brand new and doesn't disappoint.  The casino was very clean.  The rooms were very clean with a great layout.  I interacted with probably 10-20 staff besides the casino people and everyone couldn't have been more helpful, cheerful and eager to please.  It was just a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

allReviews.title: Vegas at its best !
allReviews.text: The overall quality and attention to detail are best we have seen in Las Vegas or anywhere for that matter! We typically stay at Bellagio but this was another level up of quality. Quality restaurants and fantastic lounges cannot be beat. Can’t wait to return

allReviews.title: Excellent Vegas strip hotel experience
allReviews.text: Beautiful not overly done hotel on the Vegas Strip, away from the crowds but easily accessible to key destination sites. Not too smoky, plenty of restaurants, games, pool, bars, and the like. We will return to this our newest favorite strip hotel.

allReviews.title: VERY expensive resort
allReviews.text: This resort is very nice, but over-priced for what you get.  The pool areas were crowded (one pool was closed completely) and it was hard to find lounge chairs and umbrellas.  The resort restaurants are hit or miss in terms of food quality.  Some of the details are very nice, while others seem like they weren't completely thought through.  For example, the blue plastic soap containers in the shower are hard plastic, which makes it hard to get the soap out of.  This seems like a weird, nit-picky thing to put in a review, but this resort is EXPENSIVE, so details like that matter.  The resort is quite far from the liveliness of the strip, which is bad and also good.  It was much less crowded than, say, the Bellagio but also, it doesn't offer quality enough food to make you want to eat there.

allReviews.title: Las vegas Fountainbluea Hotel not bad either.
allReviews.text: We went to Las Vegas and stayed at the Fountainbluea (across from Circus Circus).  It is at the other end of strip, but we didn't want to be in the crowd of the strip.  My husband loved this hotel from the restaurants, prominaid,  room service, the room itself,  ( it has a razor, shavingcream, toothpaste and toothbrush) NICE ROOM Royle Suite, pool and there is different one's too. Next door is Sarah's which you can catch the tram from there, also restaurants over at Sarah's too.  Bell services ( at the airport) takes you right to the door.  We got a taxi to take us to Fremont Street.   All the staff is professional and know their stuff.  I recommend that you stay here at least once it's not your average stay (hotel).

allReviews.title: Awesome Resort!
allReviews.text: What a wonderful and beautiful resort! First class in every respect! The room was immaculate and the bed and pillows were unbelievably comfortable! Excellent food and service and a great casino. Don’t miss this resort! It’s well worth checking it out!

allReviews.title: Pool!
allReviews.text: Main reason for booking was for the pool, I visit on an annual basis and I am a true Resorts World fan, but I thought I 'd give it a try. I'm sorry that I did, 2-3 of the pools were closed and therefore the others could not accommodate the guests properly. There was no music, or so low you couldn't hear it. Wait staff stated there had been complaints by "families" that the music was too loud. Family demographic is not the audience and therefore unsure why this would be accommodated over the actual demographic of people there with no children. (note: this was "end of season" Oct24). But they should've waited to turn the pools into ice rinks a week later then as they were doing nothing, one still had water in it. AND NOTE THIS ON THE WEBSITE, somewhere visible so guests are aware.Overall the property lacked character as well, it seemed very bland and stale with no personality but a bunch of "bow-ties".There are positives also. The staff was great and the room was a good size.Note: there are 2 rideshare pick ups/drop offs.

allReviews.title: Finally heading home after a fantastic stay at Fontainebleau Las Vegas!
allReviews.text: The resort was generous with promotional credits, which made my time at the slots even more fun, especially on the last night. 🎰🤘🏼 The hotel itself is stunning, with a classy, modern vibe and plenty of high-end amenities. While it is a bit north on the Strip, making people-watching less of a priority here, the distance does lend a more relaxed and refined atmosphere that’s perfect if you’re looking to escape the usual hustle and bustle.Rooms were beautiful and comfortable, and I managed to book at a really reasonable rate by keeping an eye out for deals. The dining options were excellent, with a mix of reasonably priced and high-end restaurants that add a real touch of elegance. Just a heads-up—guests definitely bring their style game at night, so if you’re heading out for a late dinner or drinks, expect to see some serious fashion statements!All in all, Fontainebleau makes for a luxurious and memorable Vegas stay, and I'd definitely come back!

allReviews.title: Recommend
allReviews.text: We found the big F a great visit, nice, clean, new recommend.  Would stay here again. Recommend Mother Wolf restaurant, and El Bagel for morning food & coffee but be prepared for a wait or order ahead on the app.  Now I am writing to hit the maximum characters to post.

allReviews.title: Don't Overthink It - Do It
allReviews.text: What a gem of a hotel.  They've transplanted the iconic style and feel of the original Miami Fontainbleau, but updated it really well.  The casino was hopping but not crazy, the jazz bar Nowhere spun 1940's post-WWII joyful vibes, and the food at Mother Wolf was transcendent.  My Noble Suite was pitch perfect with its decor and charm and mid-Century understated elegance, and all the employees were en fuego and on point.  I'm a picky and long-time Vegas lover.  Oh yeah, the fitness center was large and impressive.  This place is great.

allReviews.title: Excellent Stay. Looking forward to our next visit!
allReviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, modern, luxurious and elegant. Service was excellent, our room was pristine (like the rest of the hotel) and the atmosphere was sophisticated and fun. Less crowded than the other big hotels which was nice and relaxing, but still had enough of a crowd to give fun energy. There were so many upscale and incredibly well designed lounges and restaurants it reminded me of NYC, but  we just didn't have time to visit most of them. Highly recommend Motherwolf for dinner. Vida was good and simple for breakfast, along with more beautiful design. The pools were fun, and LIV nightclub was fun too. Excited to stay here again in December.

allReviews.title: Expected much more
allReviews.text: Disappointed:Room was (just) okay, clean etc. Plugs not in convenient spot to work at table; had to stretch them across the floor.  Lighting was also not good for working at the table.Bathroom/Shower extremely poor design.  Although shower was reasonable size, the location of the showerhead made it almost impossible to rinse the lower part of the body as the shower  stall width was too narrow.  Discussed my stay while at the airport with a stranger and he had the same problem in the shower.  Also tried running the hot water for at least 10/15 minutes multiple days and could not get hot water in the sink to shave.Was attending a conference that included food.  Overall the food was also just "okay".  Have been at many conferences on the strip in the past and I would have to say the food was nowhere near the top.  Also room labeling at the conference was not great.  Even the coffee was sub-par.Nothing like the Fontainebleau in Miami.  Expected much more here.

allReviews.title: Extraordinary on all levels
allReviews.text: Where to even start giving our experience has been fabulous. The food and beverage is fantastic as we’ve eaten on premises at several restaurants, including room service breakfast each day. I highly recommend Komodo for dinner. The self parking is free and very convenient to get in and out. The hotel is absolutely gorgeous in all respects, from the common area’s exquisite design and architecture, to the casino, to the rooms. The beds and pillows are extremely comfortable and everything is in excellent condition and good working order. We’ve had quiet nights of sleep and the fitness facility is exceptional and energizing. The equipment options could suit anyone of any age, of any condition. It’s nice that it’s not a party scene and all of the staff and guests we encountered have been very friendly.The new retail that’s opening is absolutely exquisite, and worthy of a visit on its own.

allReviews.title: Luxury Personified
allReviews.text: I initially had a reservation at Mandalay Bay, but later discovered this hotel and boy am I glad I did. The only thing better than a 5 star hotel is a brand new 5 star hotel that opened less than a year ago. Just to echo what others have written, this hotel is spectacular. Beautiful room with marble everywhere. Hi tech lighting. Incredible bathroom. Super comfortable bed. Even the hallways are beautiful- very wide with artwork on the walls. Elevators are touch screen which I’ve never seen before. The fitness center stands alone as the best hotel gym I have ever seen, and I’m an old man.  The gym is as big as a commercial gym, but has equipment that’s better than 90% of commercial gyms. All of the hotel employees are incredible. Special shoutout to Gabriel who works at the fitness center. Nothing I have said is hyperbole. It’s the truth.

allReviews.title: Shaken not Stirred
allReviews.text: First trip to the Fontainebleau Vegas was for Business, it was so nice we decided to return for pleasure. If you are looking for top shelf, pampering without the usual Vegas clutter and commotion, upscale pool vibes. Think James Bond/Sinatra old time classy vibes only. If you want oversized margaritas look elsewhere.

allReviews.title: A First Class Luxury Experience
allReviews.text: I’ve been visiting Las Vegas for over 25 years and I must say, this is the finest resort I’ve ever stayed. It was top notch from the moment I checked in. I felt like a VIP. It is so well thought out and designed. The staff is first class, friendly & very helpful. I do not miss the location south strip that is so congested and feels like a circus. I will certainly be making plans to come back very soon!

allReviews.title: Strange housekeeping situations
allReviews.text: View is great, bed is comfortable, Don's Prime is amazing!  This was our 2nd stay here and we enjoy the property however the housekeeping was subpar this time.  Upon checking in, we went to our room and it smelled as though there had been a serious sewer issue so we immediately returned to the check in desk.  The woman made a call and was told to put us in a certain room number so we went there and the room was smaller but that's okay, there are only 2 of us and we still had a great strip view.  2 days into our stay, we came back from the pool and the door would not open.  The latch that flips across the door was closed somehow and Engineering had to come open it.  He had a "tool" to open it so this must be a common issue.  Later that night when we returned to the room, a staff member was coming out of our door.  We asked her what she was doing and she brushed us off saying we were "VIP" guests so she was doing an inspection and quickly walked away.  Please note there was no other evidence or mention of a "VIP status" the entire stay and the room smelled strongly of perfume when we entered as if it had just been sprayed.  The following day, we returned from brunch around 2 and a male employee was directly outside our room, walking away.  The sink drains had been closed (we were unable to open them), water was slowly running in one sink (more than a drip), 2 garbages were still full but we had new towels and the bed had been made.  We were both feeling poorly so we climbed in bed and did not report the water/garbage issues.  We left early the next morning.  Stay was good overall, but the housekeeping situation was very odd.

allReviews.title: You won't regret staying here!
allReviews.text: Beautiful and very spacious rooms.  Excellent views with a whole wall of windows to see that view from.  An amazing giant tub 2 people could fit in, might need a step to to get in and out of lol.  Probably the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in.

allReviews.title: Very nice place to be in vacation with your friends and family
allReviews.text: This place is awesome. I will recommend this place to my friends and family. They have good drinks good comps it’s a must go! Also the view is beautiful restroom super clean my room had a tub and a shower. The housekeeping is awesome there they clean up with the room. Every day!

allReviews.title: Couples trip
allReviews.text: We only stayed 1 night at this beautiful hotel and my only regret was that we didn't stay longer. From the minute we walked through the door, the customer service was faultless. At check in, we were given 2 bottles of water each, without us having to ask.Our stunning room on the 33rd floor had a spectacular view. The room was spotlessly clean, super comfy bed and was finely appointed and decorated. Unfortunately, I didn't get a chance to enjoy the super deep soaking tub but we did enjoy an hour or 2 at the beautiful pool. Breakfast at Vida the next morning was outstanding and I would stay at this gorgeous hotel again in a heartbeat 💓 💗

allReviews.title: Beautiful resort!
allReviews.text: This was my second visit to Fontainebleau this year. I love it there!  It is a beautiful resort. The vibe is unmatched.  The decor is glamorous yet modern. The service was fantastic and the restaurants and bars are all amazing.  They even have live jazz and a piano player.  There’s something for everyone.  It is spacious and open which is nice and makes it feel more comfortable than other resorts on the strip.  The pool area is beautiful as well.  I will definitely be going back soon!

allReviews.title: Excellent Service!
allReviews.text: Our room was clean and the bed was comfortable. What really made our trip so enjoyable were some of the staff at Westgate. We'd like to call out these people for amazing service and helpfulness: Carmen Alveno at the WOW Players Club. Carmen was so patient and went "above and beyond" to be helpful. Craig at the front desk checked us in and got our trip off to a really pleasant start. Lydia at the front desk checked us out with a huge smile, pleasant coversation, and a "Happy Thanksgiving." Lastly, Jimmy the doorman, was the final smile as we left for the airport! All resort/casinos in Las Vegas have similar amenities -- but the Westgate stood out because of the people who work there!

allReviews.title: Jose Mr Westgate...great guy!!!
allReviews.text: My wife and I had finished a great dinner at Fresco. We were about to enter the theater and realized we had full glasses of wine from dinner. Jose "Mr. Westgate" saw us standing outside the theater finishing our wine. He gave us a warm welcome and told us that we could bring our wine into the concert. That NEVER happens in this town! AND we would have fired back two glasses of expensive red if he hadn't noticed us and took action. Love this guy! He's easy to find...  just look for the handsome man dressed quite dapper in his bright blue suit! I get the feeling he's the "go to" guy for all things Westgate!

allReviews.title: Fun Place to enjoy the Casino and SportsBook

Casino Manager and Dawn Rawle, VP of Marketing.  They are an Asset to the Company and take time to make me feel welcome and important..... The Resort is very clean and well maintained.

allReviews.title: Clean, comfortable and comparatively inexpensive - will stay again
allReviews.text: Stayed just one night .. went to see the Wizard of Oz at the Sphere (worth the trip btw) ... never stayed at Westgate previously but I definitely will again.   Rates were reasonable, room was spotless, comfortable, spacious, and well appointed.  Check-in was a breeze.   What really surprised me was room service .. ordered breakfast which arrived quickly, at the correct temperature (even the eggs) and was exceptionally tasty.    Parking was $10 per day and easy to access.   Entire staff was helpful with directions.   It's right next to the convention center and has a monorail station, so there is an easy, inexpensive option for traveling to the strip (although we did not use that this trip).   Only grievance was the $75 dining credit ... we stayed one night and by the time we got back from the show, all the restaurants, food court and room service options were closed (at 10pm).   Credit could not be carried over for breakfast the next day.

allReviews.title: Quick trip to Vegas

High-octane is one of the best bands we have listened to in a long time. and we are from the Rock ‘n’ Roll city Hall of Fame. They also have a fantastic guitarist and drummer. I would highly recommend taking the time to stop and sit for a while and take in all the various genres of music they can play.

allReviews.title: Outdated and staff leave you feeling unwanted.
allReviews.text: Resort tried to overcharge me close to $100 and showed me their outdated accounting terminal where the numbers didnt line up.  They grouped room cost and tax into a single item insted of itemized when I asked for a receipt for how I was being charged.  Multiple of my friends at the convention also had stories of being overcharged as well.  A lack of investment into modernization is clearly doing no good for Westgate.  The room itself is outdated, lacks many amenities that cheaper hotels offer (they treat microwaves as upgrades), I had to ask for a do not disturb sign from the front desk which is demeaning since the whole reason I want it is privacy, and certain things like the lighting just didn't work properly due to the weirdest setup ever.  The speakers on the TV were either the cheapest ever or blown out; either way it was rendered inoperable.  Oh and there was random bits of damage in multiple places to the room itself, way overdue for a renno.The staff are rude and I don't know if they were asking me personal questions to offer me timeshares or just to be judgemental but multiple times I had staff ask me too much for comfort when I was just trying to get some service to deal with issues.  Sorry, but im never going to invest in a time share, let alone when you cant even fix the issues I have right now.Then rude staff at the collection area asked for my id to take out $.50.  A level of sheer pettiness that isnt required at all.  Anything below 10k doesnt require ID in Nevada and I had clearly lost money to get that low a receipt.

allReviews.title: ⚠️ Bait-and-Switch Vacation Package – Stay FAR Away
allReviews.text: I came to Vegas expecting a relaxing getaway and booked a vacation package that included two $100 spa credits. I even triple-checked before my appointment to make sure everything was covered, and they assured me it was.After my spa service, while I was at my poker tournament, I received the full bill anyway. Despite speaking with multiple agents and managers, no one would fix it. Only then did they start mentioning some supposed tour requirement that was never disclosed anywhere.I felt completely misled and taken advantage of. Seems to be common practice at this place, just read the more reviews like mine. What should have been a smooth, enjoyable trip turned into a stressful mess. Stay far, far away from this place….. Now cue the generic unhelpful AI response.———————————————————————-“Hi There, 😏Thank you so much for sharing your feedback!👉 We really don’t care, but it’s important that we pretend we do.We’ll go ahead and copy-paste a few sympathetic sentences about how “this isn’t the experience we strive to provide” and assure you that we’ll “share it with our team” — which, of course, means no one will actually read it.We appreciate your insights, though! Please come back soon so we can disappoint you all over again — and don’t forget to join us for that 90-minute timeshare pitch we’ll swear you signed up for.Warmest robotic regards,The Auto-Apology Department 🤖“

allReviews.title: Worst hotel I've ever stayed at in the entire world
allReviews.text: There are no housekeeping services — they do not make the bed, clean the room or empty the trash the entire week — and when you call to request it, they say, "Oh, so sorry, we'll send someone right up," and then they never come. You order room service — it never comes. The elevators constantly bypass floors without stopping. To get on an elevator from the lobby up to your room, you have to wait in a line 30 feet long. One morning it took 43 minutes to get from my room to the front door of the hotel because of the elevators.Viva Cafe cannot accommodate the traffic. They need more people working there. You have to walk through disgusting cigarette smoke to get through the lobby and to the restaurants. (gag!!!) NEVER, ever, ever stay at the Westgate, no matter what. allReviews.title: Terrible time share hotel
allReviews.text: We got a free stay through Chuck E. Cheese, but it came with a required 90-minute timeshare presentation — which turned into an almost 5-hour nightmare.From the start, customer service was awful. Our shower didn’t work, and when I called down, the front desk lady acted like she didn’t believe me and had an attitude about it. After insisting, she finally sent someone to fix it.Throughout our stay, we were constantly approached by people acting like scammers, promising free gifts and perks to get us to attend another “tour.” The moment we said we already had one scheduled, they completely changed their tone and didn’t offer us anything.At the presentation, things went from bad to worse. It took over an hour just to get seated in a crowded room full of other guests being sold the same thing. They offered disgusting food — a boiled hot dog or some soupy beef with beans and bacon. While we ate, our rep acted super friendly and “interested in our lives,” but once he started his pitch, it was all high-pressure sales and made-up numbers.When the promised 90 minutes were up, I politely said we weren’t interested and wanted to leave. He said we could leave, but the “tour” wasn’t over and that we’d be charged $500 if we left early. So we stayed. After a few hours of walking around and listening to more sales talk, we were shown prices, which kept changing every time we said no. It went from thousands of dollars down to “just” $130/month — still a hard no from us.By this point, I was having a panic attack from how pushy they were. Even through tears, the rep and his manager kept pressuring us. The rep even shared our personal info with the manager to make himself look good. Then another woman came over, claiming she “wasn’t there to sell anything,” and immediately tried one last time to lock us into a trial plan for $75 down. When I refused again, she blamed my emotions on my boyfriend!Finally, after 5 hours, we were told to go get our “gift.” They sent us across the property, only for the front desk to say we weren’t getting anything because our “tour was over.”5 hours wasted. Stress. Tears. Manipulation. It completely ruined our day and the rest of our stay.Do NOT fall for the free stay or the timeshare deals. It’s not worth it unless you actually want to spend your entire day being pressured into something you don’t want. Stay far, far away from Westgate.

allReviews.title: Over priced with over aggressive time share sales people
allReviews.text: First the good: We were allowed to check-in early without being charged the early check-in fee. Got a room on 23rd floor with a very nice view of the Sphere. Room was larger than expected and clean. Front desk staff were very friendly and helpful. There is a tram stop right in front of the hotel. The casino seemed to have less smoke then most. They also had some nickel video poker games, which we enjoyed since we aren't  big gamblers.Now the bad: From the moment we stepped inside the lobby we were besieged by time share sale's people offering freebies in exchange for attending a time share presentation. They stopped us once before we got to the front desk and twice more before we made it to the elevators. We were dragging our luggage with us, so was not appreciated. The hotel had 2 "guest service" desks. Both were manned by sales people who again tried to get us to attend a sales presentation. They did not provide any service for guests.The room had a bed, but no chair for sitting. The bathroom was outdated. It had a tub shower and the shower head was coming lose from the wall.There are no reasonably priced restaurants in the resort or nearby. Every meal, including breakfast cost of $100. There is no coffee maker in the room.The hotel charged a $51 a night resort fee on top of the overpriced room.

allReviews.title: Hate the Westgate’s $25 parking fee

allReviews.title: Comfortable stay, but slightly dated decor
allReviews.text: The hotel's location is convenient, especially near the Las Vegas Convention Center. The room was large and clean, but the decor seemed a little old. The casino and sportsbook section is quite crowded, but at night there is a little more noise, so it was difficult to rest. The staff were great, but the check-in process took a while. allReviews.title: Westgate the best gate!

It’s kind of hard to leave this place when everything is just so easy to stay! Recommend this place to everyone who comes to Vegas

allReviews.title: Hotel did not honor room booking, told us we were a nuisance
allReviews.text: We booked a room with two queen beds and a sofa bed specifically because we have two older teens who wanted their own space. We confirmed this the front desk upon arrival, but when we got to the room it had one king bed and a sofa. While my wife tried to contact phone the hotel from the room, I went back to reception to see if we could change to what we had booked.We were told that we had been 'upgraded' (not really the case), and that an alternative room was not available. We specifically chose this hotel for the three bed option, so we were very disappointed to be told that my daughter would have to sleep on the floor until another room was free the next day. A mattress was requested but did not arrive until we chased it up three hours later.We assumed that the hotel would take care of the room move offered for the next day, as is the case with other establishments, but the hotel told us we would have to return between 1 and 3pm to switch. This was really inappropriate considering we wanted to have a full day out the next day.To compound our disappointment, the duty manager at the front desk complained loudly that "we were making his life difficult". He even asked us if we had heard what he said...we believe he wanted us to hear. So, not only had we not got the room we had reserved well in advance, but we were being blamed for being awkward.The hotel staff were (apart from that guy) excellent, especially at Sid's restaurant, where the breakfasts were also wonderful. However, the rooms themselves are showing signs of age, and ours had not been properly cleaned (dirty mirror, hairs in the shower and bathroom floor etc.) and no daily housekeeping was provided. in the first room the safe was broken, the sofa bed did not lie flat (friendly maintenance guy said "this happens to old beds") but at a jaunty angle, the toilet roll hold came off the wall and there weren't enough towels.The bottom line is that we would not even consider the Westgate again.

allReviews.title: Juana H made the cancellations a little bit more pleasant.
allReviews.text: My brother and I came here last Friday October the 10th to see three of the shows in the Westgate. And Juana H., from the entertainment department seated us for the first show call Jen Kramer the magic of. But unfortunately that was the only show that we did get to see that night. And it makes me extremely sad to know that if I come back in a year's time that none of those shows may be at this hotel. allReviews.title: Monorail great. Timeshare people are annoying. Need to get better security on the rooms!
allReviews.text: Not long got back from staying at Westgate. Lovely hotel, clean and the monorail is brilliant getting down to the strip! Need more food places though, as they all close pretty early. A few problems with our stay though, the joining rooms which you can hear the people staying next door as if they were right in your room. Another thing is that the security, last day of check out we had some guy banging on our door and a couple of other rooms near us, aggressively banging shouting wake up. The Westgate need to think about getting security for people to have rooms and they have to show their card every time they go upstairs like other vegas hotels. We did look out the peep hole, the person didn’t have work uniform on or a badge so we didn’t answer. Felt very unsafe that day and if it wasn’t my last day I would have been checking out that day. And the time share people are so annoying!!! No I don’t want your free breakfast.

allReviews.title: Management competency in doubt.
allReviews.text: Dated. Staff are mostly indifferent. And the competence of the management is definitely in question. Traveled here with several colleagues, and for most of us, the hotel made mistakes in one or more ways. They had the wrong check in and check out days for me. Which meant they locked me out of my room for 30 minutes while I had to get new keys made. The manager on staff refused to fix the problem at check in, and instead gave me “their word” it would be fixed. It was not fixed. They scarcely apologized. If there were any redeeming features it may be redeemable. Instead it’s standard Vegas shlock with carpet that my colleague recognized from 4 decades ago. Next time I have a conference here, I’ll stay elsewhere

allReviews.title: Closest Hotel in Las Vegas to Convention Centre
allReviews.text: Most convenient hotel if you are in Las Vegas for a convention, which we were. We upgraded our room to a "large King" so that we would ensure we had a King sized bed in our room as well as a sofa and tv area. It was worth the $35 a night upgrade. 23 rd floor- elevators are very slow and can get backed up ( during a convention) as hotel is full. There are only 3 restaurants that are open most evenings, Benihanna, Steak House and Italian. all are good average guest check $200 per couple. Casino is like all of the rest of the casinos on the strip. Never used the pool ( only open uyntil 6 p.m) and did not have time to see the show- which was not the headliner Barry Manilow, but a musical. Time share will try and give you credits and benefits for going to see presentation, but they are not too hard sell. Stores are small and some are quite aggressive, most likely they do not get much business. Walk to major hotels hotel omn the strip is about 30-40 easy walking. We would stay here again due to proximity to Convention Centre as you can walk to it from the hotel banquet rooms easily.

allReviews.title: Needs a refresh
allReviews.text: I stayed here to see Air Supply and Paul Mcartney.  If you look closely, the place needs a refresh.  I had a room on the 18th floor center tower which had a great view of the sphere.  The bath still has a tub.  There were no usb outlests anywhere in the room.  No regular outlets  by the bed or on the credenza.  No do not disturb sign to keep housekeeping out.  No kiosks for checkin.  I downloaded the app to check in and it would not add my reservation so had to wait in line for 30 min.  Service at the international bar on a Sat afternoon was slow.  The theater is getting old. Very small bar.  My seat should have been sold as partially obstructed view.  On the plus side, monorail stops and bus stop outside.  A stop for the M ride that will take you to Allegiant stadium for events.  The italian restaurant was ok but had good service.

allReviews.title: Not the one for me

With such a large resort fee, that is the part of the resort I wanted to use.There was no where near enough beds around the pool and a queue and run at 10 when it opened.I contacted them directly and heard nothing back.Otherwise, the staff when there were pleasant.

allReviews.title: The palace that elvis build
allReviews.text: The Westgate always offers a grand time..self contained you need not venture out elsewhere as it offers the pool scene, great resturants, a good sized casino and quick access to the convention center...however..if you need to get to the strip the tram is convenient and fast from the lobby.

allReviews.title: Wonderful customer service
allReviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised by my recent weekend stay at the Westgate Las Vegas made especially enjoyable due to the outstanding customer service. Specifically, the poolside service provided by Kelly Lincoln really made the day for the whole family. She was always available to help us out, and entirely pleasant, and patient, toward my large indecisive family.The second surprise was the beautiful and expansive Benihana restaurant.  A bit of a blast from the bast the large dining area is like a theme park version of a Japanese village.  There are small foot bridges, intimate dining nooks, faux rivers, and thematic lighting.  Separate areas offer everything from teppanyaki to sushi.  Our hostess at the  teppan grill was the lovely Sachi who expertly guided us through the menu and was as attentive and professional as any fine dining experience one could imagine.

allReviews.title: Didn’t get the room we paid for. Rude staff. Won’t be back.
allReviews.text: Our flight was cancelled so we were already startled and had to fly at 5am the next day. The front desk lady was extremely rude. She said we were too early and then I told her our situation and she laughed and said we were late. We didn’t get a signature king bed we paid for and she said that this is just a request and never guaranteed and it’s in the fine print. My reservation didn’t say anything about this and I’ve never experienced this in my life. I was told that we were upgraded to a 2 queen room. Having two queen beds is not an upgrade for my wife and I. We were told the king beds were sold out. I call BS and also saw them available online a few minutes later. Of course she wasn’t wearing a name tag so we didn’t know her name. Our third floor room was a view of a deteriorating roof. It was clean though. The gym had no cleaning supplies like normal gyms do. No wipes or anything to clean the equipment so people were just dripping all over the machines. The pool was nice but the overweight life guard was eating fried chicken on the job and my wife saw one of them vaping in the bathroom.  5 stars for Benihana. 5 stars for the Fishbone concert. 0 stars for the common area filthiness and the timeshare lady following us when we were already trying to avoid her. 0 stars for not being able to get noon checkout since they claimed to be sold out on a Sunday. We may come for dinner or a concert in the future but not for the hotel. And that makes sense why the Westgate has so many bad reviews.

allReviews.title: Great customer service from Craig at the owners check in.
allReviews.text: The customer service energy. Everyone on all levels were willing to help and be courteous.One particular experience was with Craig at the owners check in. He was  outstanding with a room situation we had. His professionalism and care was phenomenal especially in this day and age. We are pleased to be owners at Westgate Las Vegas! We always tell everyone about Westgate.

allReviews.title: “Westgate ruined my wedding night and refused to take responsibility.”
allReviews.text: I booked a stay at Westgate Las Vegas for what was supposed to be the most important trip of my life — my wedding. Instead, the hotel’s negligence left me devastated.Our original room (1689) had no hot water. At 1:00 AM a repairman tried and failed to fix it, and we were rushed into another room (653). The bellman quickly moved our bags but no one took inventory, and no one reminded us to check the safe. Room 1689 was still booked under my name for the full week, yet valuables — including credit cards in my name — were never returned.The hotel had every opportunity to act responsibly, but instead ignored me completely. No manager reached out. No investigation was offered. No accountability was taken.Nevada law makes it clear: hotels cannot hide behind liability limits when gross negligence occurs (Kahn v. Tropicana Hotel, Hotel Riviera v. Torres). This wasn’t just poor service — it was reckless disregard for a paying guest.Westgate’s negligence didn’t just cost me property. It cost me peace of mind. It destroyed my wedding night. And the silence afterward shows how little they value their guests.⚠️ My advice: think twice before trusting Westgate with your money, your property, or your memories.

allReviews.title: Viva Las Vegas!
allReviews.text: We had our wedding here and visit this hotel and casino a lot. Love it! From the restaurants to the amazing pool service from Irene! She is simply the best! Thank you to all the staff that make our trips excellent!

allReviews.title: High Octane

allReviews.title: GREAT SHOW!  ...RUN ...don't walk... to see Barry Manillo!
allReviews.text: Blown away by the HIGH ENERGY of BARRY MANILLO'S performance!  Loved the show from start to finish!  ....And he displayed a GENUINELY NICE personality, which was truly refreshing.   Love Vegas for the shows and HIGHLY RECOMMEND seeing BARRY MANILLO!   .......Great SPECIAL EFFECTS.  Theater staff was so helpful and friendly (which is important).  Our favorite show on this trip and we went to 6 great shows.  We recognized every single song.  I don't think there are any bad seats in the theater.  We were on the floor, in the middle, about 12 rows from stage for this show (Awesome).  We have sat in the balcony for other shows, which was fine for us as well.  I would caution anyone with mobility issues from sitting in the balcony, as there are stairs.

allReviews.title: Almost perfect
allReviews.text: We had another wonderful experience at Westgate. The room was kept in top shape , thanks to Martha Belloso and Monye’ Turner. Timothy Ham provided great guidance on our ownership options and we upgraded to the next level ❤️We experienced poor water pressure and warm water in our suite. In addition my desire to play the local golf course was thwarted once again. I have yet to play their golf course and this has been one of my greatest disappointments. As a Westgate Owner from 2003 in Florida, I remain disappointed with this recurring event. I hope to visit in 2026 when the course is open to help get them to 5 stars.  The course looks beautiful from our window but I can’t get a tee time 🏌🏿‍♂️😢

allReviews.title: Average hotel too far away from everything
allReviews.text: Stayed at Westgate for 5 nights for the Big Blues Bender in September 2025. Check in was quick and easy and front desk person was friendly. There were enough elevators that you did not have to wait long. Our room was pretty basic. It did have a fridge which was nice. The king size bed was also very comfortable. There was a large dresser in which the drawers would not stay shut.... something was not level. Bathroom was old and very basic. The tap in the bath dripped and they could not fix it. The room did have a fairly large couch in it. We were on the 10th floor and had a view of the golf course. There are not many food choices at the Westgate, especially for quick eats. We did eat at the Pub style restaurant by the sports book twice and it was pretty good. We also ate twice at the Italian place Fresco. I highly recommend this . Lots of food as wife and i shared a salad and then lasagna. food was delicious and service was good.Played some Blackjack without luck. Dealers were horrible, no smile, no interaction just take the money. They seem to forget that this is supposed to be entertaining. I don't mind losing if at least there is a little fun at the table. Stopped gambling because of this.Wife only played slots and didn't hit any wins of mention. Pool area is pretty small and was really packed with people there for the Blues Bender. The gym was quite well equipped but was really crowded.The various theatres for the music were all pretty good. Sound was very good.The biggest issue is that the Westgate is far away from most everything. It is a 1 km walk to the strip and you come out by Circus Circus. It seems like a long walk when its so hot out. That is pretty much the closed spot for other food options. You can get the monorail right at the Westgate which will take you to the strip, but its not that cheap anymore.I would not stay here unless there is something at the hotel you are coming to see.

allReviews.title: Worth giving it a try

allReviews.title: Worst Hotel Experience Ever – Stay Away
allReviews.text: We stayed at Westgate Las Vegas for 5 nights and it was a complete disaster from start to finish.First night, we were given the wrong room type (Signature instead of Luxe).Every room we were moved to smelled strongly of cigarettes.The “Luxe” room we ended up in (Room 2010) was dirty, dusty, with broken facilities.Key cards failed, leaving us locked out with our child asleep in a stroller.The toilet overflowed and flooded the bathroom while we were putting our daughters to bed.On top of all that, my wife developed severe shoulder pain from the bed and is still suffering, and our 2-year-old daughter complained of back pain from the horrible pull-out sofa.Housekeeping never fixed the dirt issue, and we were insulted with a meaningless $50 credit that did nothing to make up for the nightmare we endured.We have stayed in many hotels before, and NEVER have we experienced this many problems in one place. This is NOT a 4-star hotel – not even close.Westgate completely ruined what should have been a family vacation. Guest Relations ignored our emails, which shows how little they care about their customers.Think twice before booking here. If this is how Westgate treats its guests, I would strongly advise staying anywhere else in Las Vegas.

allReviews.title: A great hotel, but a little further out.
allReviews.text: A bit further out than the hotels on the strip, the Westgate is an excellent hotel, but has a few minor faults.   The location means much walking or taxis if the Las Vegas Strip or downtown is your thing.  Fortunately, the monorail is  very close to the hotel which is a welcome service from 7am to 3am.  The room s are good, clean, quiet and spacious.  The minor negative of the room is there are no tea and coffeee making facilities in the room meaning you have to go all the way down to Starbucks in the lobby and pay $6 for a cup of tea or Coffee before you go back to your room to start your day.  ( Probably an extra profit opportunity )   I was told these facilities are available with paying extra for an "oversized room"  All other communal areas were great, clean and well serviced.   We couldn't use the pool one Saturday because of "a private party"    We all know of the $51 per night local room tax, but that is no fault of the hotel.   Overall, a great stay with just a few negatives.

allReviews.title: Second time staying & would stay again

We stayed for 4 nights and it was great, no complaints on anything. Staff were friendly and attentive, rooms were spacious and more importantly, clean! Facilities were perfect and the added bonus of the monorail stopping exactly at the hotel and the hotel offers free shuttles to Fremont street makes the stay even better. Can’t wait to visit Vegas again and I will be staying here again. Close enough to everything you could need or want to explore, but also set back from the strip slightly which we loved. Hotel is easy enough to navigate around, casino area is also pleasant and the shops/extras on offer are plentiful. Really great experience, would recommend anyone to stay here when visiting Vegas, especially now it’s had a bit of a revamp/uplift which was needed a couple years ago.

allReviews.title: Fine for the $Cost.
allReviews.text: First the good, then the not-so-good. The bed is comfortable, and the blackout curtains work. The air conditioning takes care of the heat (which it did not when we once stayed at a much more upscale hote). The hot water is hot. There is a mini-refrigerator that works, and a hairdryer, ditto. The couch is fairly comfortable. The lighting in the room is good. There is no noise at all from the hallway, let alone the usual nighttime Vegas shrieking. There are plenty of elevators, and they come quickly.The two restaurants we have tried: Rikki Tikki Sush is fantastic. The Italian restaurant is very good. This is what made me shift from 3 stars to 4.The staff are a lot of fun, from our check-in guy (who remembered us two days later) to the bartenders and servers.The not so good: the air conditioning is too cold so has to be turned off, then it gets hot. There is a lighted makeup mirror but is does not show your face. The bathroom area is primitive, and the shower has no hand-held. There are no safety grab bars for old people like me. Restaurants (for example the Asia Bistro) seem to be closed a lot on weekdays. allReviews.title: Nightmare at the Westgate
allReviews.text: Absolutely — here’s a strongly worded (yet still professional and impactful) negative review you could use:⸻⭐️ 1 Star — Absolutely unacceptable experience at the Westgate Las VegasIf I could give zero stars, I would. Our pool team is here for a 2-week stay, and from the moment we arrived, it’s been nothing but problems.First — no hot water. Not just for a day. It’s been days without a single warm shower. Try spending all day at a tournament and coming back to an ice-cold rinse every night — and then being told “we’re working on it.” No timeline. No updates. allReviews.title: 2 Stars- Don’t Bother Staying Here

The bathroom sink was clogged and we had to request maintenance to come up to snake it.The “Safe” was locked and we were told we had to remain in the room for security to come up since the previous guests had left their passports, wallet, and monies in the safe and we “had to be present “ during the security retrieval, while they opened the safe.The vanity lighted mirror in the bathroom was coming off the wall and didn’t work.We reported that as well and maintenance had to come twice to repair the issue.The closet door to the safe had been broken by previous guests and needed Maintenance to Bring tools to repair it as well!What happened to supervisory room checking before releasing rooms to new guests?The entrance door to our room was dirty and hadn’t been wiped down for who knows how long?! I got out bacterial wipes and wiped it down as well.We requested the night before departure to have bell desk send up assistance when we were leaving the last day and was assured they would come up at 10am the following morning-they even wrote a note and placed it with a sticky note on their bell desk-however-We were stood up-no one ever showed.I complained to the manager about all these issues as well as the poor communication with staff and customer service.We WON’T be back to THIS HOTEL ever again.It is outdated, unkept, and poor service to guests.To Kevin- Manager At Front Desk-Extremely Disappointed-in spite of our attendance to the Event at your property-there’s no excuse for the poor quality of service we experienced- especially after speaking to YOU before our stay and anticipating your utmost care thatDid Not Transpire.

allReviews.title: Still A Great Vacation Destination
allReviews.text: We came here this year for our thirty- year wedding anniversary. We became timeshare owners at Westgate in 2006 because the resort is beautiful and very well maintained. The rooms are furnished in a modern contemporary way. They are clean, comfortable,  and roomy. We have a 4 bedroom that we upgraded to when we went to Vegas for the first time in 2020. The Vegas resort is their crown jewel and it is every bit that. I judge every place I go to by the cleanliness of their restrooms and the Westgate resorts restrooms are top-notch from one location to the next. The resort has many things to do while you are on the resort grounds and they provide free shuttle service to and from nearby venues. If I could change one thing that is a sore sticking point with me it would be the hours of the fitness center which are currently a depressing 6am - 6pm. REALLY? We hail from the east coast and we are all fitness nuts, my wife, son, and daughter. I would have expected the hours to change from the last time I was here and complained about it but they have not as of this review.It has now been 5 years since I upgraded my timeshare to Las Vegas.I hope I don't have to wait much longer. I also miss the all-you-can-eat buffet that they have/ had, but it has only been opened on weekends. I don't know if it is open any longer but the food was great. They have other great four our five star restaurants that you can eat at if you like. They also have at least one 24- hour bistro spot and convenience store across from each other. I don't gamble much but they have a nice compliment of slots and gaming tables on the casino floor. I sat around the sports book area for a while and was impressed. There is so much to do in Vegas that you cannot do it all in a week. You have to pace yourself, have a plan, and listen to recommendations by others about things to do, eat, and places to go.I had a great conversation with one of their knowledgeable security personnel. It was refreshing to speak with someone on Westgate's staff that could tell you more about the resort and Vegas.

allReviews.title: Westgate Legal Scam - don't fall!
allReviews.text: I only stayed at Westgate because the Salsa Super Congress was being hosted here. They were running a “special promotion” which seemed affordable — until I realized I was signing up for a one-lifetime-subscription-for-regret.The “90-minute” Presentation = Half Your Day GoneThis was advertised as a quick 90-minute presentation. In reality? Expect to spend 2–3 hours minimum. They check you in, make you wait in the lobby, ask you to eat before starting (why?), then bring you into an endless upsell loop where one “manager” after another tries to get you to buy their product.When you say no, they won’t let you leave.They literally block you with sales tactics and pressure. Because of this nonsense, I missed my entire morning plan, including a long-anticipated visit to The Sphere.This isn’t a “presentation” — it’s a lifetime subscription to regret. Please don’t fall for it.No Security on Guest FloorsThere is no keycard access or security on guest room floors. I received multiple flyers for massage and pizza discounts slid under my door every single day — clearly from random people walking through the hotel halls. That’s not safe. Any outsider can just take the elevator up.This made me feel very uncomfortable during my stay.Toothpaste… Costs Extra?I called for toothpaste and was told I had to buy it at the gift shop. Why does a so-called 4-star hotel charge for basic hygiene items?Late Checkout = $45I asked to check out just 30 minutes later (11:30 AM instead of 11), and they said it would be $45. Seriously?Aggressive Vibes All AroundFrom the staff to the overall vibe, everything here feels like a hard sell. It honestly feels like, because I got a discounted room rate through the promo, I was nickel-and-dimed at every step — toothpaste, late checkout, everything costs extra.No warmth, no hospitality. Just relentless selling and marketing.I will never stay here again. The only reason I came this time was because the Salsa Congress was here — and that event was amazing.But the hotel? Never again.

allReviews.title: Want to be disappointed, disrespected and ripped off. Stay at the Westgate
allReviews.text: I was VERY disappointed with my recent stay at the Westgate Resort & Casino. I was attracted to stay there because of the low room price. However, on arrival I was charged an extra $300 amenities fee, of which, only $100 was refundable. What a SCAM!!! Charge a PRE PAY low price for the room and pay an extra $200 when you get there. If you say I'm not going to stay here they keep the PRE PAY amount as well. The staff were also a disappointment, they were a mix of most helpful to very discourteous. When I arrived the valet was helpful until he found out I wanted to self park, Then he refused to tell me where the self park garage was and just pointed to a sign. As a guest at the hotel I expected to park at a reduced rate of for free. No such luck! The hotel nickel dimed another $45 for the privilege. When  I finally got into the room I was disappointed to find that it was not as well appointed as other in which I have stayed.Most hotel rooms not have a small coffee maker in the room so you do not have to get dressed and get that all important first cup. The Westgate charges $5 for a cup of their regular coffee just outside of the casino. There was also no microwave in the room which room which is also standard in most hotels these days. There was a refrigerator in the room, (I guess it's there so the overpriced beverages sold in the many gift shops throughout the resort can be kept cold). The next disappointment came when I tried to take a shower the next morning and wound up standing in a foot and one half of water. The bathtub drain was plugged. (The resort did fix that sometime during the day while I was out). I had signed up for a Grand Canyon tour which left from the Sahara Resort the next day. The Sarhara is located several blocks away from the Westgate. The tour leaves at 5 AM but no one on the staff of the Westgate could tell me how to get there. There advice was, "You'll have to take a taxi." I will admit that taxi got me there in three minutes but I could have easily walked that distance in 10 minutes if someone on the staff of the Westgate pointed me in the right direction.  On the positive side the room was very clean, comfortable, and cool in which to sleep.
